description: The accountable authority must govern the entity in a way that: (a) promotes the proper use and management of public resources; (b) promotes achievement of the entity's purposes; and (c) promotes financial sustainability.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must govern the NDIA in a way that: (a) promotes the proper use and management of public resources; (b) promotes achievement of the NDIA's purposes; and (c) promotes financial sustainability.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 19(1)
description: The accountable authority must: keep the responsible Minister informed of entity activities; provide reports, documents and information as required; notify the Minister of significant decisions; give reasonable notice of significant issues; and notify as soon as practicable after becoming aware of significant issues affecting the entity.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must: keep the responsible Minister informed of NDIA activities; provide reports, documents and information as required; notify the Minister of significant decisions; give reasonable notice of significant issues; and notify as soon as practicable after becoming aware of significant issues affecting the NDIA.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 22(3)
description: If a Government Policy Order applies to the NDIA, the accountable authority must ensure the order is complied with in relation to the entity and, so far as practicable, any subsidiary.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: If a Government Policy Order applies to the NDIA, the accountable authority must ensure the order is complied with in relation to the NDIA and, so far as practicable, any subsidiary.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 35
description: The accountable authority must prepare a corporate plan at least once each reporting period covering the entity's purposes, operating environment, performance measures and activities, including for any subsidiaries. The plan must be given to the responsible Minister and Finance Minister.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must prepare a corporate plan at least once each reporting period covering the NDIA's purposes, operating environment, performance measures and activities, including for any subsidiaries. The plan must be given to the responsible Minister and Finance Minister.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 37
description: The accountable authority must cause records to be kept that properly record and explain the entity's performance in achieving its purposes. Records must enable preparation of annual performance statements.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must cause records to be kept that properly record and explain the NDIA's performance in achieving its purposes. Records must enable preparation of annual performance statements.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 38
description: The accountable authority must measure and assess the performance of the entity in achieving its purposes, in compliance with requirements prescribed by the PGPA Rule.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must measure and assess the performance of the NDIA in achieving its purposes, in compliance with requirements prescribed by the PGPA Rule.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 39
description: The accountable authority must prepare annual performance statements for inclusion in the entity's annual report, reporting on the entity's performance against its purposes as set out in the Corporate Plan.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must prepare annual performance statements for inclusion in the NDIA's annual report, reporting on the NDIA's performance against its purposes as set out in the Corporate Plan.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 45
description: The accountable authority must ensure the entity has an audit committee with functions including reviewing the appropriateness of the entity's financial reporting, performance reporting, systems of risk oversight and management, and systems of internal control.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must ensure the NDIA has an audit committee with functions including reviewing the appropriateness of the NDIA's financial reporting, performance reporting, systems of risk oversight and management, and systems of internal control.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013 s 46
description: The accountable authority must prepare an annual report for the entity in accordance with the PGPA Rule. The report is presented to the responsible Minister for tabling in Parliament.
applicability: Applies because NDIA officials use public resources and must make ICT decisions with proper governance, integrity and accountability. Means for the NDIA: The accountable authority must prepare an annual report for the NDIA in accordance with the PGPA Rule. The report is presented to the responsible Minister for tabling in Parliament.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
applicability: Direct. Applies to all NDIA integrations, especially those exchanging participant, provider, partner or other government data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
applicability: Direct. Applies to NDIA-owned systems, shared integration platforms, partner connections and provider-managed services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
applicability: Direct. Relevant where NDIA connects to partner, provider, state, territory, Commonwealth or whole-of-government services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
applicability: Direct. Applies to integration platforms, API gateways, managed services, SaaS connectors, middleware, data exchange services and support providers.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
applicability: Direct. Applies to all contracts and outsourcing arrangements that design, build, host, operate, support or connect to NDIA integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
applicability: Direct. Applies to vendors, contractors, subcontractors, delivery partners and managed service providers supporting NDIA integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
applicability: Direct. Applies to all third-party and partner integrations, including API, file transfer, messaging, event, data replication and support channels.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
applicability: Conditional direct. Applies when NDIA consumes outsourced ICT services, shared government services or government-provided integration platforms.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct. Applies to integration providers and support contracts throughout planning, onboarding, operation, change and exit.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
applicability: Direct. Applies to all partner, provider and outsourced integration arrangements.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
applicability: Direct. Applies to integration procurements, cloud or managed services, SaaS connectors, APIs and providers with offshore ownership, hosting, support or subcontracting.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct. Applies to all third-party and outsourced integrations while they remain connected to NDIA systems or data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
applicability: Direct. Applies to integration platforms, API products, connectors, gateways, libraries, managed services, partner endpoints and provider services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 07. Countering Foreign Interference and Espionage
description: Entities manage the security risks associated with engaging with foreign partners.
applicability: Conditional direct. Applies where NDIA integrates with foreign partners, foreign-hosted services or arrangements involving foreign access to NDIA data or systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
applicability: Conditional direct. Applies where integrations generate, route, ingest or exchange email messages, notifications or email-based data transfers.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
applicability: Direct where integration data is security classified; good-practice baseline for sensitive NDIA data classifications and metadata mapping.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
applicability: Conditional. Applies where NDIA needs to categorise information by access restrictions or downstream use limitations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
applicability: Direct for classified information and highly relevant to sensitive participant, provider and government information exchanged with external entities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: The Memorandum of Understanding between the Commonwealth, States and Territories is applied when sharing information with state and territory government agencies.
applicability: Conditional direct. Applies to NDIA integrations with state and territory government agencies and services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
applicability: Direct for integrations sharing security classified information outside government; recommended for sensitive information shared with providers and partners.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Provisions are met concerning the security of people, information and resources contained in international agreements and arrangements to which Australia is a party.
applicability: Conditional. Applies to NDIA integrations involving international agreements or arrangements.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign entity is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional. Applies where NDIA integrations could disclose Australian Government security classified information to foreign entities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
applicability: Conditional. Applies if NDIA integrations process, transmit or expose AUSTEO information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
applicability: Conditional. Applies if NDIA integrations process, transmit or expose AGAO-caveated information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Where an international agreement or arrangement is in place, security classified foreign entity information or resources are safeguarded in accordance with the provisions set out in the agreement or arrangement.
applicability: Conditional. Applies where NDIA receives, processes or exchanges security classified foreign entity information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign non-government stakeholder is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional. Applies to integrations with foreign non-government providers, partners, suppliers or stakeholders involving security classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
applicability: Direct. Applies to APIs, middleware, event platforms, message queues, file transfer, gateways, network connections, data pipelines and integration support tooling.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Direct. Applies to all new, changed and existing integrations proportionate to risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
applicability: Direct. Applies before go-live for each integration system, platform, reusable service or material data flow.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
applicability: Direct. Applies to new integrations, new partner connections, significant changes and control exceptions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
applicability: Direct. Applies to integration platforms, API gateways, data hubs, event buses, managed file transfer services, databases and logs.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
applicability: Direct. Applies to integration platforms, services, gateways, connectors and external data exchanges that are part of NDIA's technology estate.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
applicability: Direct. Applies when integrations undergo significant functional, architectural, hosting, connectivity, partner, classification or control changes.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
applicability: Direct where legacy interfaces, protocols, middleware, certificates, network paths or partner services remain in use.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: A Protective Domain Name System service or other security mechanisms is used to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints.
applicability: Direct. Applies to internet-connected APIs, gateways, partner endpoints, data transfer services, webhooks, middleware and cloud integration services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
applicability: Direct. Applies to cloud-hosted integration platforms, SaaS integration connectors, API management, gateways, managed file transfer and cloud middleware.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Direct. Applies to IRAP-assessed cloud, gateway, managed services and shared platforms used by NDIA integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Security classified or systems of government significance information and data is securely hosted using a Cloud Service Provider and Data Centre Provider that has been certified against the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
applicability: Conditional direct. Applies where integrations process, store or communicate security classified information or systems-of-government-significance data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: The Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel is used when procuring certified data centre space and services.
applicability: Conditional. Applies when NDIA procures certified data centre capacity, hosting or colocation for integration infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Internet-connected technology systems, and the data they process, store or communicate, are protected by a gateway in accordance with the ISM and the Gateways Policy.
applicability: Direct. Applies to public APIs, internet-connected data exchanges, partner/provider connections, cloud ingress or egress paths and externally reachable services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Gateways or Secure Service Edges that have completed an IRAP assessment (or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways) against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
applicability: Direct. Applies to gateways, Secure Service Edge services, cloud security gateways, cross-domain gateways and managed gateway services used by integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: A vulnerability disclosure program and supporting processes and procedures are established to receive, verify, resolve and report on vulnerabilities disclosed by both internal and external sources.
applicability: Direct. Applies to public APIs, developer portals, integration platforms, webhooks, externally accessible services and provider-facing interfaces.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A Technology Asset Stocktake and Technology Security Risk Management Plan is created to identify and manage the entity's internet-facing systems or services to ensure continuous visibility and monitoring of the entity's resource and technology estate.
applicability: Direct. Applies to internet-facing APIs, gateways, partner portals, webhooks, data exchange services and integration management planes.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Approved post-quantum cryptographic encryption algorithms are used for newly procured cryptographic equipment and software in accordance with the ISM's guidelines for cryptography.
applicability: Direct for newly procured integration cryptographic equipment and software; important for APIs, TLS termination, gateways, certificates, key management and data transfer.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Digital Infrastructure that processes, stores or communicates Australian Government security classified information is protected by a Gateway or Security Service Edge in accordance with the Australian Government Gateway Security Standard.
applicability: Conditional direct. Applies where digital infrastructure supporting NDIA integrations processes, stores or communicates Australian Government security classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Connect to the Australian Signals Directorate's Cyber Threat Intelligence Sharing platform.
applicability: Direct where NDIA security monitoring supports CTIS connectivity; relevant to cyber operations protecting integration services.

reference: Fraud and Corruption Rule - regular risk assessments

reference: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework - awareness, reporting and response

publisher: Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre / Attorney-General's Department

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs Division 1 - value for money
description: Officials must achieve value for money when procuring goods and services.
applicability: Applies where CPRs are triggered or adopted; also supports PGPA proper use of public resources for NDIA.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs Division 1 - efficient, effective, economical and ethical procurement
description: Procurement must be conducted ethically and support efficient, effective and economical use of public resources.
applicability: Applies to NDIA ICT sourcing, renewals, extensions, panels, managed services and cloud arrangements when CPRs or internal procurement rules apply.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs accountability and transparency requirements
description: Entities must maintain appropriate records and accountability for procurement decisions and contracts.
applicability: Applies to ICT procurement records and contract management evidence for NDIA services.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs Division 2 - additional rules for procurements above relevant thresholds
description: Additional requirements apply to covered procurements, including open competition and conditions for limited tender.
applicability: Applies when ICT procurements meet CPR coverage and threshold triggers.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs and contract management expectations
description: Procurement obligations extend into contract management through monitoring, records, performance and risk management.
applicability: Applies to NDIA managed service providers, system integrators, cloud providers and ICT support contracts.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act 1988 section 15 and Schedule 1 APP 1
description: Agencies must not breach the APPs and must manage personal information in an open and transparent way.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA as an agency handling personal and sensitive information.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 3 and APP 5 - collection and notification
description: Personal information must be collected only where reasonably necessary and individuals must be notified about collection matters.
applicability: Applies to participant, provider, staff and stakeholder information collection through ICT services.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 6 and APP 8 - use, disclosure and cross-border disclosure
description: Personal information can only be used or disclosed for permitted purposes, with controls for overseas disclosure.
applicability: Applies to NDIA data sharing, reporting, analytics, support access, cloud services and suppliers.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 10 and APP 13 - quality and correction
description: Agencies must take reasonable steps to ensure personal information is accurate, up-to-date and complete, and allow correction where required.
applicability: Applies to systems of record, master data, case management, portals and integration services.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11 - security of personal information
description: Agencies must take reasonable steps to protect personal information and destroy or de-identify it when no longer needed, subject to records obligations.
applicability: Applies to production, testing, reporting, backup, archive and supplier environments holding personal information.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 12 - access to personal information
description: Individuals have rights to access personal information held about them, subject to exceptions.
applicability: Applies to ICT services that hold information needed for privacy access requests, participant channels and casework.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code sections 6 and 7
description: The Code sets specific requirements agencies must comply with as part of APP 1.2 and is binding on agencies.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA as an Australian Government agency subject to the Privacy Act.

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code section 9 - Privacy Management Plan
description: Agencies must have a privacy management plan and measure annual performance against it.
applicability: Applies to ICT services and projects that handle personal information or privacy risks.

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code sections 10 and 11 - Privacy Officer and Privacy Champion
description: Agencies must designate a Privacy Officer and Privacy Champion with specified functions and leadership responsibilities.
applicability: Applies to ICT service governance, incident escalation, PIAs, complaints and access/correction support.

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code section 12 - Privacy Impact Assessments
description: Agencies must conduct a PIA for all high privacy risk projects or initiatives.
applicability: Applies to ICT projects, service changes, integrations, data migrations and supplier transitions that may significantly affect personal information handling.

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code section 15 - PIA register
description: Agencies must maintain and publish a register of completed PIAs.
applicability: Applies to ICT initiatives subject to PIAs.

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code sections 16 and 17 - training and review
description: Agencies must provide privacy training and regularly review privacy practices, procedures and systems.
applicability: Applies to NDIA ICT staff, contractors, service desks, developers, operations teams and suppliers with access to personal information.

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: Privacy Act Part IIIC - Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
description: Entities must notify affected individuals and the OAIC about eligible data breaches.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA because it is subject to the Privacy Act and handles personal and sensitive information.
source: Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC / Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: Privacy Act section 26WE - eligible data breach
description: An eligible data breach generally involves unauthorised access, unauthorised disclosure or loss of personal information likely to result in serious harm.
applicability: Applies to cyber incidents, misdirected communications, data loss, supplier incidents, unauthorised access and system errors involving NDIA personal information.
source: Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC / Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: Privacy Act section 26WK - assessment of suspected eligible data breach
description: Entities must take reasonable and expeditious steps to assess a suspected eligible data breach, generally within 30 days.
applicability: Applies to all suspected privacy-impacting ICT incidents and supplier incidents.
source: Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC / Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: Privacy Act sections 26WL and 26WM - statement and notification
description: Where notification is required, entities must prepare a statement for the Commissioner and notify affected individuals or at-risk individuals.
applicability: Applies when NDIA determines an ICT incident is an eligible data breach.
source: Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC / Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: OAIC data breach preparation and response guidance
description: Entities are expected to prepare data breach response plans and roles before incidents occur.
applicability: Applies across NDIA ICT operations and managed service providers.
source: Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC / Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act 1982 section 11 - right of access
description: Members of the public have a legally enforceable right to obtain access to agency documents, subject to exemptions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA documents and records held in ICT services, ticketing systems, email, collaboration platforms and supplier repositories.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and FOI Guidelines

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act Part II and section 8 - Information Publication Scheme
description: Agencies must publish required information, including an agency plan and specified operational information.
applicability: Applies to NDIA online publication platforms and information assets covered by IPS requirements.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and FOI Guidelines

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act section 10 - operational information
description: Agencies must publish operational information used in making decisions or recommendations affecting members of the public.
applicability: Applies to policy, process, workflow, guidance and decision-support information managed through ICT services.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and FOI Guidelines

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act section 11C - disclosure log
description: Agencies must publish certain information released in response to FOI access requests within required timeframes.
applicability: Applies to NDIA web and records systems used for FOI disclosure log publication.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and FOI Guidelines

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act section 93A and OAIC FOI Guidelines
description: Agencies must have regard to the FOI Guidelines when performing FOI Act functions.
applicability: Applies to ICT service records and publication processes supporting NDIA FOI administration.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and FOI Guidelines

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Archives Act 1983 sections 24 and 26
description: Commonwealth records must not be destroyed, disposed of or altered except as authorised under the Act and records authorities.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA public records held in ICT systems and service management tools.
source: Archives Act 1983, records authorities and records management policy
publisher: National Archives of Australia / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: National Archives records authorities
description: Records authorities are legal instruments authorising retention, destruction or transfer of Australian Government records.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA ICT systems and service management repositories that hold Commonwealth records.
source: Archives Act 1983, records authorities and records management policy
publisher: National Archives of Australia / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Building Trust in the Public Record - Action 1
description: Agencies must assess information management capability.
applicability: Applies to NDIA as a corporate Commonwealth entity covered by the Building Trust policy.
source: Archives Act 1983, records authorities and records management policy
publisher: National Archives of Australia / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Building Trust in the Public Record - Action 9
description: Agencies must manage digital information assets created from 1 January 2016 digitally, unless a valid exception applies.
applicability: Applies to digital information assets created and managed by NDIA ICT services.
source: Archives Act 1983, records authorities and records management policy
publisher: National Archives of Australia / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Archives Act 1983

description: Agencies must identify records of national archival value and plan transfer to the National Archives.
applicability: Applies where NDIA systems hold archival-value records or enduring Scheme records.
source: Archives Act 1983, records authorities and records management policy
publisher: National Archives of Australia / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025

name: Digital Experience

applicability: Applies to ICT service roadmaps, remediation plans and accessibility improvement programs.
source: Disability Discrimination Act 1992 and AHRC digital accessibility guidance
publisher: Australian Human Rights Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Commonwealth legislation / accessibility and non-discrimination obligation

name: Electronic Transactions Act 1999
reference: Electronic Transactions Act 1999 section 8
description: A transaction is not invalid merely because it took place by means of electronic communication.
applicability: Applies to NDIA electronic forms, approvals, notices, correspondence and service requests unless an exclusion applies.
publisher: Attorney-General's Department / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Commonwealth legislation / electronic transaction validity obligation

name: Electronic Transactions Act 1999
reference: Electronic Transactions Act sections 9-12
description: Legal requirements for writing, signature, production and retention can be met electronically if specified conditions are satisfied.
applicability: Applies to digital forms, approvals, acknowledgements, consents, records and evidence created through NDIA ICT services.
publisher: Attorney-General's Department / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Commonwealth legislation / electronic transaction validity obligation

name: Electronic Transactions Act 1999
reference: Electronic Transactions Act section 14 - time and place of dispatch and receipt
description: The Act contains rules for determining when and where electronic communications are dispatched and received.
applicability: Applies to portals, email, workflow systems, messaging, notifications and API transactions.
publisher: Attorney-General's Department / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Commonwealth legislation / electronic transaction validity obligation

name: Electronic Transactions Act 1999
reference: Electronic Transactions Act section 15 - attribution
description: Electronic communications may be attributed to a person in specified circumstances.
applicability: Applies to identity, access management, digital signatures and user account controls in NDIA services.
publisher: Attorney-General's Department / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Commonwealth legislation / electronic transaction validity obligation

name: Electronic Transactions Act 1999
reference: Electronic Transactions Act exclusions and consent requirements
description: Some laws, documents or transactions may be excluded or require recipient consent to electronic communication.
applicability: Applies to service design for notices, decisions, consents, records and communications under NDIS and other laws.
publisher: Attorney-General's Department / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Commonwealth legislation / electronic transaction validity obligation

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act 2024 section 3 - objects
description: The Act establishes a secure, convenient, voluntary, accessible and inclusive Digital ID framework.
applicability: Conditionally applies to NDIA services that rely on or integrate with Digital ID services.
source: Digital ID Act 2024, Digital ID Rules 2024 and Digital ID privacy safeguards

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act 2024 - accreditation framework
description: Entities providing Digital ID services can be accredited and must meet requirements.
applicability: Applies if NDIA procures, integrates with or relies on accredited Digital ID services.
source: Digital ID Act 2024, Digital ID Rules 2024 and Digital ID privacy safeguards

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act 2024 and Digital ID Rules 2024 - Australian Government Digital ID System
description: The Act and Rules establish governance and participation requirements for the AGDIS.
applicability: Applies if NDIA participates in AGDIS or relies on AGDIS-enabled identity flows.
source: Digital ID Act 2024, Digital ID Rules 2024 and Digital ID privacy safeguards

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID privacy safeguards and OAIC Digital ID role
description: Digital ID has specific privacy safeguards in addition to Privacy Act obligations.
applicability: Applies to identity proofing, attribute exchange, authentication events and user account linking.
source: Digital ID Act 2024, Digital ID Rules 2024 and Digital ID privacy safeguards

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID incident and fraud controls
description: Digital ID services require security, fraud and incident management controls.
applicability: Applies to authentication failures, account takeover, identity fraud, enrolment errors and supplier incidents.
source: Digital ID Act 2024, Digital ID Rules 2024 and Digital ID privacy safeguards

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 - DATA Scheme
description: The Act establishes a scheme for safe sharing of Australian Government data to improve services, policies and research.
applicability: Conditionally applies when NDIA shares or receives data under the DATA Scheme.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner
type: Commonwealth legislation / data sharing scheme obligation

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme permitted purposes
description: Data sharing must be for one of the permitted purposes: government services, government policies and programs, or research and development, and must meet public interest and other tests.
applicability: Applies to NDIA data sharing arrangements under the Scheme.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner
type: Commonwealth legislation / data sharing scheme obligation

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme accreditation and data sharing agreements
description: Participants must meet accreditation and agreement requirements before sharing scheme data.
applicability: Applies where NDIA acts as or works with a data custodian, accredited user or accredited data service provider.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner
type: Commonwealth legislation / data sharing scheme obligation

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme reporting requirements
description: Scheme entities have event-based, change, annual and scheme data breach reporting obligations.
applicability: Applies to NDIA scheme data sharing arrangements, breaches, material changes and annual reporting.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner
type: Commonwealth legislation / data sharing scheme obligation

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme interaction with privacy, secrecy and records laws
description: Data sharing does not remove obligations under other applicable laws, including privacy and secrecy requirements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA data sharing where NDIS protected information or personal information is involved.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner
type: Commonwealth legislation / data sharing scheme obligation

name: Responsible AI
reference: Responsible AI Policy v2.0 - application and mandatory requirements
description: The policy sets mandatory requirements for accountable officials, transparency statements, strategic approach, operations, use case accountability, registers, training and impact assessment for in-scope agencies.
applicability: For NDIA as a corporate Commonwealth entity, apply where adopted, directed, funded through relevant processes or required by internal policy; use as baseline for AI services.
source: Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government and AI Technical Standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: Responsible AI Policy - accountable official(s) and use case accountability
description: Agencies must designate accountable officials and assign accountability for AI use cases.
applicability: Applies to NDIA AI use in service management, digital channels, analytics, decision support or automation.
source: Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government and AI Technical Standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: Responsible AI Policy - transparency statements and internal use case registers
description: Agencies must maintain transparency and register AI use cases as required.
applicability: Applies to AI-supported service desk, chat, triage, analytics, content generation, decision support and workflow automation.
source: Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government and AI Technical Standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: Responsible AI Policy - staff training and operationalising responsible AI
description: Agencies must train staff and operationalise responsible AI practices.
applicability: Applies to staff and contractors who procure, configure, operate, monitor or use AI in ICT services.
source: Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government and AI Technical Standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI Technical Standard - AI system lifecycle statements
description: The technical standard covers operational model, architecture, data, training, evaluation, integration, deployment, monitoring and decommissioning.
applicability: Applies to AI-enabled services, embedded AI features and AI models used by NDIA or suppliers.
source: Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government and AI Technical Standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: Responsible AI Policy - AI use case impact assessment
description: In-scope AI use cases require impact assessment according to policy criteria.
applicability: Applies to NDIA AI use cases, especially those affecting users, sensitive data, service access, risk scoring or prioritisation.
source: Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government and AI Technical Standard

name: Commonwealth Child Safe Framework
reference: Commonwealth Child Safe Framework - purpose and coverage
description: The Framework sets minimum standards to create and maintain child-safe cultures and practices in Commonwealth entities.
applicability: For NDIA as a corporate Commonwealth entity, apply as recommended/adopted baseline given NDIA services for children and young people.
type: Commonwealth framework / child safety compliance requirement

name: Commonwealth Child Safe Framework
reference: Child Safe Framework Requirement 1 - annual child safety risk assessment
description: Entities must undertake annual risk assessments to identify risk of harm to children and young people and appropriate strategies.
applicability: Applies to NDIA digital services, channels and records involving children and young people.
type: Commonwealth framework / child safety compliance requirement

name: Commonwealth Child Safe Framework
reference: Child Safe Framework Requirement 2 - training and compliance mechanisms
description: Entities must establish training and compliance mechanisms for people who engage with children or material related to children.
applicability: Applies to ICT staff, contractors and suppliers with access to child-related data or services.
type: Commonwealth framework / child safety compliance requirement

name: Commonwealth Child Safe Framework
reference: Child Safe Framework Requirement 3 - National Principles for Child Safe Organisations
description: Entities must adopt and implement the National Principles for Child Safe Organisations as appropriate.
applicability: Applies to NDIA ICT services interacting with children, families, nominees, carers and providers.
type: Commonwealth framework / child safety compliance requirement

name: Commonwealth Child Safe Framework
reference: Child Safe Framework Requirement 4 - annual statement of compliance
description: Entities must publish an annual statement of compliance with the Framework.
applicability: Applies where NDIA reports child-safe compliance or adopts equivalent reporting.
type: Commonwealth framework / child safety compliance requirement

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage and outsourced network/hosting services; conditional where NDIA provides services to other entities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
source: PSPF Direction 001-2024 - Managing Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence Risks to Technology Assets

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: A business continuity plan is developed, implemented and maintained to respond effectively and minimise the impacts of significant business disruptions to the entity's critical services and assets.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud Compute and Storage; Hardware Portfolio where assets support critical services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Plans for managing a broad range of emergencies are integrated within the business continuity plan.
applicability: Directly applicable - all three scope areas where disruption affects NDIA critical services or assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure stores, processes or communicates security classified or caveated information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud/SaaS email services; Hardware Portfolio where endpoint/email clients are managed.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage and systems storing classified information; Networks where metadata travels across services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage repositories and platforms where access restrictions are recorded or enforced.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 10. Information Holdings
description: Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 11. Information Disposal
description: OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and Cloud Compute and Storage; Networks where logs or configurations contain NDIA information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 11. Information Disposal
description: Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure stores, processes or communicates security classified or caveated information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The TikTok application is prevented from being installed, and existing instances are removed, on government devices, unless a legitimate business reason exists.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and managed endpoints; Networks and Cloud through access controls and app/service blocking.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The CSO or CISO approves any legitimate business reason for the use of the TikTok application on government devices and ensures specified mitigations are in place.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and managed endpoints; Networks and Cloud through exception monitoring and controls.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets and their components, classified as SECRET or below are stored in the appropriate Security Zone based on their aggregated security classification or business impact level.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and network/security appliances; Cloud/Data Centre where NDIA manages physical components.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets and their components classified as TOP SECRET are stored in suitable SCEC-endorsed racks or compartments within an accredited Security Zone Five area.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure handles TOP SECRET information, systems or components.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Outsourced facilities that house technology assets and their components with a catastrophic business impact level are certified by ASIO T4 physical security and accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional - applies to outsourced data centre or facility services housing catastrophic-BIL technology assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the Information Security Manual.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and storage media; Cloud where provider-managed assets store NDIA data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: A cyber security strategy and uplift plan is developed, implemented and maintained to manage the entity's cyber security risks in accordance with the ISM and the Guiding Principles to Embed a Zero Trust Culture.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Patch applications mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Patch operating systems mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Restrict Microsoft Office macros mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio/endpoints and SaaS productivity environments; supporting control for networks/cloud.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: User application hardening mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Regular back-ups mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage; Hardware and Networks for systems, configurations and logs.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: The remaining mitigation strategies from the Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents are considered and, where required, implemented to achieve an acceptable level of residual risk for their entity.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: A Protective Domain Name System service or other security mechanisms is used to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and cloud connectivity; Hardware Portfolio for managed endpoints.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage; Networks for cloud connectivity and Secure Service Edge services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage, data centres, gateways and managed network services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Security classified or systems of government significance information and data is securely hosted using a Cloud Service Provider and Data Centre Provider that has been certified against the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
applicability: Conditional - Cloud Compute and Storage and data centre hosting where information is security classified or declared SOGS.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: The Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel is used when procuring certified data centre space and services.
applicability: Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage/data centre services; Hardware and Networks for hosted infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Internet-connected technology systems, and the data they process, store or communicate, are protected by a gateway in accordance with the ISM and the Gateways Policy.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and internet-connected hardware/cloud systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Gateways or Secure Service Edges that have completed an IRAP assessment (or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways) against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and cloud Secure Service Edge; conditional for TOP SECRET gateways.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: A vulnerability disclosure program and supporting processes and procedures are established to receive, verify, resolve and report on vulnerabilities disclosed by both internal and external sources.
applicability: Directly applicable - internet-facing Networks and Cloud services; Hardware where externally reachable management interfaces exist.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Approval for remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems in international locations is only granted if approved by the Australian Signals Directorate.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where NDIA permits international remote access to TOP SECRET systems or data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions to allow personnel to work remotely in international locations.
applicability: Directly applicable - remote administration/access to Networks, Cloud and managed devices from international locations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel are not granted approval to work remotely in locations where Australian Government information or resources are exposed to extrajudicial directions from a foreign government that conflict with Australian law, unless operationally required.
applicability: Conditional - applies to international remote work or administration involving NDIA infrastructure or information resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: Separating personnel have their access to Australian Government resources withdrawn upon separation or transfer from the entity.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Protective security is integrated in the process of planning, selecting, designing and modifying entity facilities for the protection of people, information and resources.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: A facility security plan is developed for new facilities, facilities under construction or major refurbishments of existing facilities.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Decisions on entity facility locations are informed by considering the site selection factors for Australian Government facilities.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: When designing or modifying facilities, the entity secures and controls access to facilities to meet the highest risk level to entity resources.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Facilities are constructed in accordance with the applicable ASIO Technical Notes to protect against the highest risk level.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
