description: Facilities for Security Zones Two to Five that process, store or communicate security classified information and resources are constructed in accordance with the applicable sections of ASIO Technical Notes.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure stores, processes or communicates security classified or caveated information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Entity facilities are operated and maintained in accordance with Security Zones and Physical Security Measures and Controls.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Security Zones One to Four are certified by the Certification Authority in accordance with the PSPF and applicable ASIO Technical Notes before they are used operationally.
applicability: Applicable where NDIA uses or controls Security Zone One to Four infrastructure spaces.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Security Zone Five areas that contain TOP SECRET security classified information or aggregated information are certified by ASIO T4 before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure handles TOP SECRET information, systems or components.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Security Zones One to Five are accredited by the Accreditation Authority before they are used operationally, on the basis that the required security controls are certified and the entity determines and accepts the residual risks.
applicability: Applicable where NDIA uses Security Zones One to Five for ICT infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility areas used to secure and access TOP SECRET systems and security classified compartmented information are accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional - applies to Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility areas used for TOP SECRET infrastructure access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to minimise or remove the risk of information and physical asset resources being made inoperable or inaccessible, or being accessed, used or removed without appropriate authorisation.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to protect entity resources, commensurate with the assessed business impact level of their compromise, loss or damage.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to minimise or remove the risk of harm to people.
applicability: Directly applicable - infrastructure facilities, server rooms, network rooms and hardware handling activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: The appropriate container, safe, vault, cabinet, secure room or strong rooms is used to protect entity information and resources based on the applicable Security Zone and business impact level.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and physical storage of media/devices; Cloud/Data Centre where NDIA controls storage.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Perimeter doors and hardware in areas that process, store or communicate security classified information or resources are constructed and secured in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Applicable where NDIA controls facilities or rooms processing, storing or communicating classified information/resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Access by authorised personnel, vehicles and equipment to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Applicable where NDIA controls or consumes facilities in Security Zones One to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Access by visitors to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for access control for visitors.
applicability: Applicable where NDIA controls or consumes facilities in Security Zones One to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: The Accountable Authority or CSO approves ongoing (or regular) access to entity facilities for people who are not directly engaged by the entity or covered by the terms of a contract or agreement.
applicability: Directly applicable - provider, contractor and facilities personnel accessing ICT spaces.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Unauthorised access to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for security alarm systems.
applicability: Applicable where NDIA controls or consumes facilities in Security Zones One to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Security guard arrangements in Security Zones One to Five are established in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for security guards.
applicability: Applicable where risk assessment requires guards for ICT facilities or security zones.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Technical surveillance countermeasures for Security Zones One to Five are established in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Conditional - applies to Security Zones One to Five where threat/risk assessment requires TSCM.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A Technology Asset Stocktake and Technology Security Risk Management Plan is created to identify and manage the entity's internet-facing systems or services to ensure continuous visibility and monitoring of the entity's resource and technology estate.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud Compute/Storage; Hardware Portfolio where assets are internet-facing or support services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Approved post-quantum cryptographic encryption algorithms are used for newly procured cryptographic equipment and software in accordance with the ISM's guidelines for cryptography.
applicability: Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks and Cloud services using cryptographic equipment or software.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Digital Infrastructure that processes, stores or communicates Australian Government security classified information is protected by a Gateway or Security Service Edge in accordance with the Australian Government Gateway Security Standard.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud connectivity for classified information; Hardware where systems connect across security domains.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Connect to the Australian Signals Directorate's Cyber Threat Intelligence Sharing platform.
applicability: Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud; Hardware Portfolio for monitored assets and endpoints.
source: PSPF Direction 003-2024 - Supporting Visibility of Cyber Threat

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Declared Systems of Government Significance are protected in accordance with the Australian Government Systems of Government Significance Standard.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure or services are declared Systems of Government Significance.

name: PSPF Directions 2024
reference: Direction 001-2024 - Managing Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence Risks in Technology Assets
description: Requires Australian Government entities to identify indicators of FOCI risk relating to procurement and maintenance of technology assets, and manage/report those risks.
applicability: Applies to NDIA ICT supplier selection, maintenance arrangements, managed services, cloud hosting and hardware supply chains where the Direction applies or as a protective security baseline.
source: PSPF Direction 001-2024 - Managing Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence Risks to Technology Assets

name: PSPF Directions 2024
reference: Direction 002-2024 - Technology Asset Stocktake
description: Requires a stocktake of all internet-facing systems or services to identify and actively manage vulnerable technology risks.
applicability: Applies to public web services, APIs, cloud endpoints, DNS, email, remote access, partner interfaces and managed gateways.

name: PSPF Directions 2024
reference: Direction 003-2024 - Supporting Visibility of the Cyber Threat
description: Requires Australian Government entities to participate in ASD's Cyber Security Partnership Program and, where using threat intelligence sharing platforms, to share cyber threat information with ASD.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cyber threat monitoring and information sharing arrangements where the Direction applies or as a baseline.
source: PSPF Direction 003-2024 - Supporting Visibility of Cyber Threat

name: PSPF Directions 2024
reference: Direction 004-2025 - Commonwealth Technology Management
description: Requires Australian Government entities to adhere to the Commonwealth Technology Standard for products, applications and web services used within government entities.
applicability: Applies to products, applications and web services used by NDIA where the Direction/Standard applies or is adopted as baseline.

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, s118 - Functions of the Agency
description: The NDIA must deliver the NDIS, support participant choice and control, promote high-quality supports, manage financial sustainability, prevent and respond to misuse or abuse, and collect/analyse/exchange data about disability and supports.
applicability: Applies directly because the NDIA is established by and performs functions under the NDIS Act.

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, Chapter 4, Part 2 - Privacy; ss60-68 protected information and disclosure provisions
description: The Act restricts unauthorised recording, use and disclosure of protected information and establishes circumstances for authorised disclosure.
applicability: Applies to NDIA information holdings and to officials, contractors and service providers handling protected information for the Agency.

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
description: The Rules support safeguarding privacy of information held by the Agency and set rules for disclosure of information.
applicability: Applies where NDIA systems store, process, communicate or enable access to protected information.
source: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, functions relating to financial sustainability and managing risks/issues
description: The Agency must manage and report on the financial sustainability of the NDIS and identify and manage relevant risks and issues.
applicability: Applies to NDIA infrastructure investments, ongoing cloud consumption and technology asset lifecycle decisions.

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, Agency function to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to misuse, abuse or criminal activity
description: Infrastructure must enable fraud detection, investigation support, access logging and evidence preservation.
applicability: Applies where infrastructure supports participant, provider, payment, analytics or investigation systems.

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, principles on accessible communication and participation
description: The Scheme is built around participant access, choice and control, and information must be communicated in suitable modes and terms where required.
applicability: Applies to infrastructure that hosts, secures or enables participant-facing and staff-facing digital channels.

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013, s15 - Duty to govern the Commonwealth entity
description: The accountable authority must govern the entity in a way that promotes proper use and management of public resources, achievement of purposes and financial sustainability.
applicability: Applies to NDIA accountable authority and officials making infrastructure decisions.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013, s16 - Duty to establish and maintain systems relating to risk and control
description: The accountable authority must establish and maintain appropriate systems of risk oversight, risk management and internal control.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA risk governance for infrastructure assets and services.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013, s17 - Duty to encourage cooperation with others
description: Accountable authorities must encourage officials to cooperate with others to achieve common objectives where practicable.
applicability: Applies to inter-agency and partner connectivity, shared platforms and cross-government infrastructure arrangements.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act 2013, ss25-29 - General duties of officials
description: Officials must act with care and diligence, in good faith and for a proper purpose, and must not misuse position or information.
applicability: Applies to NDIA employees, officials and relevant contractors performing ICT infrastructure functions.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: Finance guidance on spending money and commitments
description: Officials need authority before entering arrangements or committing relevant money, and approvals must be recorded in writing.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA ICT commitments, renewals, consumption increases and contractual changes.
source: PGPA Act 2013 governance and compliance guidance

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Rule 2014 - audit committee and risk/internal control review expectations
description: The audit committee reviews the appropriateness of risk oversight, management and internal control systems.
applicability: Applies to NDIA reporting on ICT controls, cyber risk, major outages, asset lifecycle risk and material supplier risks.
source: PGPA Act 2013 governance and compliance guidance

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: NDIA procurement guidance - non-prescribed corporate Commonwealth entity status
description: The NDIA states it is a non-prescribed Commonwealth Corporate Entity and that the Government Procurement Judicial Review Act 2018 does not apply to NDIA procurements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA ICT procurement policy framing and contract governance.
source: NDIA procurement and grants guidance - PGPA context

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10 - Fraud and Corruption Rule
description: The Rule sets minimum standards for accountable authorities of PGPA Act entities to manage the risk and incidents of fraud and corruption.
applicability: Applies to NDIA as a PGPA Act entity. The broader Fraud and Corruption Policy is binding for NCEs and better practice for CCEs, but the Rule is binding for all PGPA Act entities.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - Fraud and Corruption Rule

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: Framework Element 1 - Fraud and corruption risk assessments
description: Entities should identify, understand and document fraud and corruption exposures and control arrangements.
applicability: Applies to high-value, high-risk or sensitive NDIA ICT infrastructure activities.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: Framework Element 2 - Fraud and corruption control plans
description: Control plans document, communicate, manage and monitor treatment of identified risks.
applicability: Applies to NDIA infrastructure portfolios and projects with material procurement, supplier or asset risks.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - Fraud and Corruption Guidance

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: Framework Element 5 - Prevention
description: Prevention is the most efficient and cost-effective way to minimise fraud and corruption risk.
applicability: Applies to procurement, receiving, acceptance, change approval, cloud consumption increases and disposal authorisations.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: Framework Element 6 - Detection
description: Entities need mechanisms to identify possible fraud and corruption incidents.
applicability: Applies to cloud usage, network services, hardware inventory, vendor invoices and privileged access activity.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - Fraud and Corruption Guidance

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: Framework Element 7 - Investigation and other responses
description: Entities must have arrangements for investigating and responding to fraud and corruption incidents.
applicability: Applies to suspected misuse involving ICT systems, suppliers, hardware or network/cloud services.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - Fraud and Corruption Guidance

name: Fraud and Corruption
reference: Framework Element 8 - Recording and reporting
description: Entities need records and reporting for fraud and corruption risks and incidents.
applicability: Applies to NDIA hardware lifecycle, secure disposal, lost assets and supplier returns.
source: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
description: The Privacy Act protects individuals and regulates how Australian Government agencies handle personal information. The APPs set requirements for personal information management.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA personal information holdings and to service providers handling that information for NDIA.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 1 - Open and transparent management of personal information
description: APP entities must manage personal information in an open and transparent way, including governance, practices and procedures.
applicability: Applies to cloud services, SaaS platforms, logs, backups, telemetry and network security services that handle personal information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 6 - Use or disclosure of personal information
description: Personal information may only be used or disclosed for permitted purposes or where an exception applies.
applicability: Applies to partner links, vendor support channels, monitoring platforms, collaboration platforms and data transfers.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 8 - Cross-border disclosure of personal information
description: APP entities must take steps before disclosing personal information overseas unless an exception applies.
applicability: Applies to all cloud, SaaS, backup, monitoring and support arrangements with potential offshore access or storage.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11.1 - Security of personal information
description: APP entities must take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA infrastructure handling personal information, including logs and backups.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11.2 - Destruction or de-identification when no longer needed
description: APP entities must take reasonable steps to destroy or de-identify personal information no longer needed, unless retention is legally required.
applicability: Applies to storage lifecycle, backup retention, media sanitisation, asset disposal and decommissioning.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Part IIIC - Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
description: The NDB scheme requires notification to affected individuals and the OAIC for eligible data breaches.
applicability: Applies to breaches involving NDIA personal information in cloud, network, endpoint, logging or backup environments.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 12 and APP 13 - Access to and correction of personal information
description: Individuals have rights to access and correct their personal information subject to the APPs.
applicability: Applies to storage systems, archives, backups, SaaS platforms and identity records holding personal information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s7 and s8 - Agencies bound and APP 1.2 compliance
description: The Code is binding on agencies and sets out how APP 1.2 must be complied with.
applicability: Applies to NDIA as an Australian Government agency handling personal information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s9 - Privacy management plan
description: An agency must have a privacy management plan and measure performance against it at least annually.
applicability: Applies to infrastructure controls that implement or evidence NDIA privacy goals.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s10 and s11 - Privacy Officer and Privacy Champion
description: An agency must have a designated Privacy Officer and Privacy Champion with defined governance functions.
applicability: Applies to major cloud, network, monitoring, remote access, endpoint and hardware disposal decisions.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s12 - Privacy impact assessments
description: An agency must conduct a PIA for all high privacy risk projects involving new or changed handling of personal information likely to significantly impact privacy.
applicability: Applies to new or changed infrastructure services that affect personal information collection, holding, access, disclosure or retention.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s15 - Register of PIAs
description: An agency must maintain and publish a register of PIAs it conducts.
applicability: Applies to PIAs completed for NDIA infrastructure initiatives.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s16 - Privacy education and training
description: Agencies must include privacy training in induction and take reasonable steps to train staff with access to personal information annually.
applicability: Applies to NDIA infrastructure staff, contractors and managed service personnel with access to personal information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: APP Code, s17 - Regular review of internal privacy processes
description: Agencies must regularly review and update privacy practices, procedures and systems and monitor compliance.
applicability: Applies to ongoing operation and review of infrastructure services that handle personal information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives guidance
description: Australian Government business information that entities create, send and receive is considered a Commonwealth record.
applicability: Applies to NDIA official records in cloud platforms, network systems, hardware asset repositories and service management tools.
source: National Archives guidance - compliant destruction of Australian Government information
type: Records management guidance under Archives Act

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Archives Act 1983 - disposal requires authority
description: Disposal includes destruction, custody/ownership transfer, damage or alteration, and destruction must be approved by National Archives, required by legislation or covered by normal administrative practice.
applicability: Applies to decommissioning, migration, backup expiry, storage deletion and disposal of media or devices.
source: National Archives guidance - compliant destruction of Australian Government information
type: Records management guidance under Archives Act

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: National Archives guidance - checks before destruction
description: Before destroying information, agencies should ensure the minimum retention period is met, the record is no longer required, the sentence is current and no disposal freeze, legal proceeding, inquiry or access request applies.
applicability: Applies to cloud retention jobs, storage lifecycle rules, backups, snapshots, hardware sanitisation and destruction.
source: National Archives guidance - compliant destruction of Australian Government information
type: Records management guidance under Archives Act

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Archives Act 1983 - records in digital systems
description: Digital information and metadata must remain reliable, accessible and usable for the required retention period.
applicability: Applies to cloud storage, SaaS, logs, configuration repositories and network management tools.
source: National Archives guidance - disposing of information
type: Records management guidance under Archives Act

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: National Archives guidance - destruction records
description: Agencies should maintain details of what information was destroyed, when, how and under which records authority.
applicability: Applies to approved data deletion, backup destruction, media sanitisation and hardware destruction.
source: National Archives guidance - compliant destruction of Australian Government information
type: Records management guidance under Archives Act

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: PSPF and Archives interaction for information holdings
description: Information and data created, sent or received by government entities is subject to the Archives Act and must be managed with operational controls proportionate to value and sensitivity.
applicability: Applies to infrastructure documentation and operational records.

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act 1982, s3 - objects of the Act
description: The FOI Act gives members of the public rights of access to official documents of the Commonwealth and its agencies.
applicability: Applies to NDIA documents stored in cloud services, logs, collaboration tools, storage platforms and contractor systems.

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act 1982, s6C - Commonwealth contracts
description: Certain Commonwealth contracts must include provisions enabling access to documents held by contractors or subcontractors relating to the performance of the contract.
applicability: Applies to outsourcing, managed services, SaaS, hosting and support contracts where FOI access provisions are required.

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act 1982 and National Archives disposal checks
description: Records should not be destroyed when affected by a current FOI access application.
applicability: Applies to data deletion, retention expiry, storage decommissioning, media sanitisation and backup destruction.
source: National Archives guidance - compliant destruction of Australian Government information
type: Records management guidance under Archives Act

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: OAIC FOI Guidelines issued under s93A
description: Agencies and ministers must have regard to the FOI Guidelines when performing functions or exercising powers under the FOI Act.
applicability: Applies to NDIA infrastructure teams responding to FOI searches or preservation requests.
source: FOI Guidelines issued under s93A of the FOI Act
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act 1982 - Information Publication Scheme and operational information
description: The Act establishes proactive publication obligations for agency information and operational information.
applicability: Applies to infrastructure policies, standards, operating models and service descriptions that may be published or requested.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD Information Security Manual - risk management framework
description: The ISM is a cyber security framework applied using an organisation's risk management framework to protect IT and operational technology systems from cyber threats.
applicability: Applies to NDIA infrastructure, including outsourced systems and cloud services, as the technical security control baseline.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight maturity model - implementation approach
description: Organisations should identify a target maturity level, progressively implement maturity levels, minimise exceptions, document/approve exceptions and monitor them regularly.
applicability: Applies to NDIA systems in scope of Essential Eight controls, especially internet-connected IT networks.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: PSPF Requirements 0099 and 0100 - patching applications and operating systems to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two
description: Patching of applications and operating systems must meet Essential Eight Maturity Level Two requirements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA servers, cloud workloads, network management systems, endpoints, appliances and provider-managed platforms where in scope.
source: PSPF Release 2025 - Essential Eight cyber security requirements

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: PSPF Requirement 0101 - multi-factor authentication to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two
description: MFA must be implemented to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
applicability: Applies to infrastructure administration, VPN/remote access, cloud management, SaaS administration and privileged support pathways.
source: PSPF Release 2025 - Essential Eight cyber security requirements

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - restrict administrative privileges
description: Administrative privileges should be restricted, controlled and monitored.
applicability: Applies to administrators, service accounts, break-glass accounts, vendor support and managed service access.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - application control and user application hardening
description: Application control and hardening reduce malware and exploitation pathways.
applicability: Applies to servers, endpoints, administrator workstations, jump hosts and management tools.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM Guidelines for Networking and Gateways
description: The ISM includes guidance for network design/configuration, wireless networks, gateways, firewalls, proxies and content filtering.
applicability: Applies to NDIA networks, cloud connectivity, SD-WAN, VPN, internet gateways, email gateways and partner links.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM Guidelines for System Monitoring
description: The ISM includes guidance on event logging and monitoring.
applicability: Applies to cloud control planes, workloads, network devices, gateways, identity systems, endpoints and security platforms.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM Guidelines for Data backup and restoration
description: The ISM includes guidance on backups and restoration as part of system management.
applicability: Applies to cloud workloads, SaaS data where export/backup is required, infrastructure configurations and critical management systems.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM Guidelines for Cryptography
description: The ISM includes guidance for cryptographic algorithms, protocols, TLS, SSH, S/MIME and IPsec.
applicability: Applies to cloud storage, network links, VPNs, APIs, management interfaces, hardware encryption and backup encryption.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM Guidelines for IT equipment and media sanitisation, destruction and disposal
description: The ISM includes guidance for IT equipment usage, maintenance, sanitisation, destruction and disposal, and media disposal.
applicability: Applies to laptops, servers, storage, removable media, network devices, mobile devices, printers and security appliances.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: Hosting Certification Framework - Government Customers
description: All Australian Government data must be hosted with appropriate privacy, sovereignty and security controls under the Whole-of-Government Hosting Strategy.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud hosting, IaaS/PaaS/SaaS hosting, data centres and managed hosting arrangements.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF requirement from 30 June 2022
description: All new and extensions to existing hosting contracts must be with Certified Service Provider(s), subject to exemptions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA hosting, cloud tenancy, data centre, managed hosting and service extensions.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF certification levels - Strategic, Assured and Uncertified
description: Certification level depends on government customer risk profile, data classification/sensitivity and internal risk assessment.
applicability: Applies to classification and risk assessment of NDIA workloads and datasets before hosting selection.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF Certified Strategic level
description: Strategic Certification is the highest assurance level and allows ownership and control conditions to be specified.
applicability: Applies to sensitive or high-impact cloud workloads, gateways and hosting for protected data.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF procurement guidance
description: Procurement should specify the required certification level and request the provider's certification ID.
applicability: Applies to NDIA requests for proposal, contracts, renewals and service catalogues involving hosting.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF certification maintenance
description: Certified providers must maintain certification, including annual review and minimum mandatory requirements.
applicability: Applies to ongoing supplier management for NDIA hosting and cloud providers.

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF reform notice
description: HCF certification registration for prospective providers and supplementary assessments has been paused from 3 November 2025 during reforms, while existing certified providers are not impacted.
applicability: Applies to new NDIA procurements and provider changes during reform period.

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025
description: The standard covers Australian Government gateways and boundaries between the internet and government networks.
applicability: Applies to NDIA internet gateways, cloud gateways, remote access gateways, email gateways, proxies and partner connectivity boundaries.

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: ASD Gateway Security Guidance - gateway delivery models
description: Gateways may be on-premises, cloud-native, hybrid or managed services and include capabilities such as remote work, external service provision and information exchange.
applicability: Applies to current and future NDIA gateway architectures and cloud connectivity patterns.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - accountability and system authorisation
description: Government organisations cannot transfer accountability to a third-party gateway provider; gateway systems require risk-based authorisation.
applicability: Applies to provider-managed internet gateways, cloud security edge, secure service edge, VPNs and managed firewall services.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - select IRAP-assessed managed gateways
description: Best practice includes selecting IRAP-assessed managed gateway solutions.
applicability: Applies to managed gateway services and cloud gateway capabilities procured by NDIA.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - HCF Strategic hosting for gateway services up to PROTECTED
description: Gateway services up to PROTECTED should be hosted by HCF Certified Strategic facilities and services.
applicability: Applies to gateway services handling OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED information where applicable.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - supply chain assessment
description: Consumers should review IRAP reports and security collateral including SRMP/SSP, bill of materials/software bill of materials and critical components/services.
applicability: Applies to gateway products, managed services, network security appliances and cloud security services.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - integration with SOC/SIEM, incident response and health monitoring
description: Gateway implementation should integrate with monitoring, incident response and organisational assurance processes.
applicability: Applies to NDIA gateways, proxies, firewalls, remote access, web/email gateways and cloud edge services.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - continuous assurance
description: Best practice includes vulnerability management, change management, ongoing risk management, configuration management and penetration testing.
applicability: Applies to operational management of NDIA gateway capabilities.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Australian Government Gateway Security Standard 2025 and ASD Gateway Security Guidance
reference: Gateway guidance - visibility for recursive resolvers, web proxies, mail relays, reverse proxies and remote access
description: Security visibility should be prioritised for key gateway capabilities.
applicability: Applies to NDIA DNS, web proxy, email gateway, reverse proxy, remote access and internet egress services.
source: ASD Gateway Security Guidance Package - Executive Guidance

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - effective 1 July 2026
description: The policy sets requirements for entities planning digital investments involving cloud computing and comes into effect on 1 July 2026.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud digital investments, cloud migration and cloud service operations subject to the policy.

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy Requirement 3 - adopt cloud technologies responsibly and securely
description: Entities must define clear roles and responsibilities for cloud oversight, delegations and internal accountabilities.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud platforms, cloud workloads, SaaS and managed cloud services.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy Requirement 3 - comply with relevant legislation, standards and frameworks
description: Cloud solutions must comply and align with Privacy Act/APPs, Disability Services and Inclusion Act, PSPF including FOCI Direction, HCF, ISM, ASD Cloud Security Guidance and APS Net Zero.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA cloud solutions and SaaS services.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy Requirement 2 - interoperability and portability
description: Entities must design for interoperability and portability to minimise vendor lock-in, including negotiating removal of clauses restricting migration of government data/workloads where possible.
applicability: Applies to IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, data platforms, backups and integration services.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy Requirement 3 - monitoring, logging and reporting
description: Entities must establish real-time, continuous monitoring, logging, analysis and reporting systems for demand, performance, security threats and continuous improvement.
applicability: Applies to cloud management planes, workloads, security services, SaaS logs and performance telemetry.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy Requirement 3 - service levels
description: Entities must define and monitor key performance and reliability metrics to ensure cloud-based services meet required standards and SLAs.
applicability: Applies to cloud-hosted NDIA business services, platform services and SaaS.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy Requirement 3 - exit strategies and data migration plans
description: Entities must prepare exit strategies and data migration plans to reduce risk and cost of future transitions.
applicability: Applies to all material cloud, SaaS and hosting arrangements.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Cloud policy - cost management and visibility
description: The policy requires cloud cost management, including transition costs, operational costs, consumption models and visibility of usage and unit economics.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud accounts, subscriptions, SaaS licences, storage and data transfer charges.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Cloud policy - Cloud Marketplace, panels and reuse
description: Entities should use appropriate cloud marketplaces/panels and reuse existing government cloud patterns where possible.
applicability: Applies to NDIA acquisition of cloud services and enabling technologies.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Policy Requirements

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Cloud policy - strategic cloud documentation
description: The policy includes requirements to develop strategic documentation for cloud.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud strategy, cloud operating model and cloud control framework.

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
description: The Act prohibits discrimination on the ground of disability in areas including employment, access to premises, goods, services and facilities, and administration of Commonwealth laws and programs.
applicability: Applies to NDIA as a Commonwealth agency, service administrator and employer.

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Disability Services and Inclusion Act 2023 for assistive technology compatibility
description: The cloud policy requires cloud solutions to comply and align with the Disability Services and Inclusion Act 2023 for assistive technology compatibility.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud-hosted systems, SaaS tools, identity flows and collaboration platforms.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - accessibility and inclusion alignment

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Digital Inclusion Standard - Criterion 4 Make it accessible
description: Australian Government digital services should apply relevant legislation, WCAG and the Australian Government Style Manual.
applicability: Applies to infrastructure supporting participant-facing services, staff services and digital channels.
source: Digital Inclusion Standard - Criterion 4: Make it accessible

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: DDA and inclusive workplace/service access obligations
description: Hardware, peripherals and endpoint standards can affect equal participation and reasonable adjustment.
applicability: Applies to desktops, laptops, mobile devices, collaboration hardware, printers, kiosks and other end-user technology.

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: DDA and remote access/service access
description: Network services and security controls should not unnecessarily restrict accessible communication modes or assistive technologies.
applicability: Applies to remote access, network filtering, collaboration platforms and secure connectivity controls.

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
description: The SOCI Act creates a framework for managing critical infrastructure assets and related obligations.
applicability: Applicability to NDIA depends on whether NDIA owns, operates, has a direct interest in, or uses services connected to a critical infrastructure asset or business critical data trigger.

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI Act - critical data storage or processing assets
description: The data storage and processing sector is regulated where assets meet statutory criteria, including services provided to responsible entities for critical infrastructure assets involving business critical data.
applicability: Applies to NDIA supplier due diligence and contract requirements where providers are SOCI-regulated or may become regulated.
source: SOCI Act data storage and processing obligations

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI Act, s12F(3) provider notification obligation
description: If a responsible entity for a critical infrastructure asset becomes aware a commercial data storage or processing service relates to business critical data, it must take reasonable steps to inform the provider as soon as practicable.
applicability: Applies only if NDIA is a responsible entity or otherwise holds business critical data connected to SOCI obligations.
source: SOCI Act data storage and processing obligations

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI Act - incident and government assistance powers
description: The SOCI framework includes obligations and government powers relating to cyber incidents affecting critical infrastructure assets.
applicability: Applies where NDIA or its providers are SOCI-regulated or support regulated assets/services.

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI risk management program considerations
description: Responsible entities for applicable critical infrastructure assets may need critical infrastructure risk management programs and annual reporting.
applicability: Applies to NDIA only if relevant SOCI asset/responsible-entity obligations are triggered; otherwise use for supplier assurance.

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security Act 2024, Part 3 and s27 - ransomware/cyber extortion payment reporting
description: A reporting business entity that makes, or is aware another entity has made on its behalf, a ransomware or cyber extortion payment must report to government within 72 hours.
applicability: Applicability to NDIA should be legally confirmed. Applies directly if NDIA is a reporting business entity or if a supplier makes a payment on NDIA's behalf.
source: Ransomware and cyber extortion payment reporting guidance

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Ransomware payment reporting guidance - active from 30 May 2025
description: Mandatory ransomware and cyber extortion payment reporting is active from 30 May 2025 for reporting business entities.
applicability: Applies to NDIA or providers if the reporting entity criteria are met.
source: Ransomware and cyber extortion payment reporting guidance

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security (Security Standards for Smart Devices) Rules 2025
description: The Rules introduce mandatory cyber security standards for most smart devices acquired in Australia by a consumer from 4 March 2026.
applicability: Applies to in-scope smart devices supplied into Australia; NDIA should require supplier evidence where devices are relevant connectable products.
source: Cyber Security (Security Standards for Smart Devices) Rules 2025

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security Act 2024 - secure technology framework
description: The Act enables mandatory security standards for smart devices to uplift baseline device security.
applicability: Applies to NDIA hardware standards and network onboarding of smart, IoT, AV, building, health or accessibility devices.

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security Act 2024 - cyber incident review and information sharing framework
description: The Act includes measures for limited-use information sharing and post-incident reviews of significant cyber incidents.
applicability: Applies if NDIA participates in voluntary sharing or is involved in a significant incident review.

name: Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy and APS Net Zero 2030 technology obligations
reference: Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy - ICT goods from 1 July 2025
description: From 1 July 2025, the ESP Policy applies to ICT goods procurements at or above $1 million, along with other high-impact categories.
applicability: Applies to NDIA ICT goods procurements that meet applicable thresholds and entity applicability; confirm with procurement/legal due NDIA CCE status.
publisher: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

name: Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy and APS Net Zero 2030 technology obligations
reference: ESP Policy - products should minimise greenhouse gas emissions, be safe for the environment and retain value for longer
description: The policy aims to reduce environmental impact and support a net zero, circular economy.
applicability: Applies to hardware standards, refresh cycles, leasing, reuse, repair, resale and disposal strategies.
publisher: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

name: Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy and APS Net Zero 2030 technology obligations
reference: APS Net Zero 2030 Target - computing and data systems
description: The Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy includes practical actions to reduce emissions from sources including computing and data systems.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud strategy and supplier assurance where government operations/net zero policies apply.

name: Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy and APS Net Zero 2030 technology obligations
reference: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - APS Net Zero alignment
description: Cloud solutions must align with APS Net Zero Emissions by 2030 as part of responsible cloud adoption.
applicability: Applies to cloud procurement, cloud operations, hosting, data centre use and hardware lifecycle management.
source: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - sustainability alignment

name: Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy and APS Net Zero 2030 technology obligations
reference: ESP Policy - APS entities and suppliers required to demonstrate compliance
description: The ESP Policy page states APS entities and suppliers are required to undertake activities to prove environmental claims and demonstrate compliance with the ESP Policy.
applicability: Applies to in-scope hardware suppliers and NDIA procurement records where the ESP Policy applies.
publisher: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
description: The Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of their entity.
applicability: Direct - applies to all NDIA application, infrastructure and data portfolio decisions with material security risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
description: A Chief Information Security Officer is appointed to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security for the entity's most critical technology resources.
applicability: Direct - the CISO must be engaged for cyber risk impacts across the ICT portfolio.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
description: The Chief Information Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber security risks and how the entity's cyber security program is managing these risks.
applicability: Direct - supports CISO accountability for the cyber security program and most critical technology resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
description: The Accountable Authority approves security governance arrangements that are tailored to the entity's size, complexity and risk environment.
applicability: Direct - applies to NDIA portfolio boards, architecture forums, investment gates and rationalisation decisions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
description: A security plan is developed, implemented and maintained to address the mandatory elements of the plan.
applicability: Direct - portfolio planning must incorporate security plan commitments affecting ICT assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
description: The Accountable Authority approves the entity's security plan.
applicability: Supporting - TPP provides ICT inputs and evidence for approved security planning.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
description: The security plan is considered annually and reviewed at least every two years to confirm its adequacy and ability to adapt to shifts in the entity's risk, threat or operating environment.
applicability: Direct - NDIA technology roadmaps and prioritisation must be reviewed at least annually and when major risk changes occur.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
description: Procedures are developed, implemented and maintained to ensure all elements of the entity's security plan are achieved.
applicability: Direct - portfolio procedures should show how PSPF-related actions move through intake, prioritisation and delivery.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
description: Develop, establish and implement security monitoring arrangements to identify the effectiveness of the entity's security plan and establish a continuous cycle of improvement.
applicability: Direct - monitoring should be embedded in portfolio dashboards and lifecycle reviews.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 04. Protective Security Reporting
description: The annual protective security report is provided to the entity's Minister.
applicability: Supporting - NDIA portfolio records should feed entity-level PSPF reporting to ministers and oversight bodies.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 04. Protective Security Reporting
description: The annual protective security report is submitted to the Department of Home Affairs.
applicability: Supporting - applies to the evidence and data outputs from NDIA ICT portfolio management.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 04. Protective Security Reporting
description: The Accountable Authority approves the entity's annual protective security report and confirms that they have verified the report's content.
applicability: Supporting - ICT portfolio owners must validate evidence used in entity reporting.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 04. Protective Security Reporting
description: Entities cooperate with the Department of Home Affairs' assurance activities to review annual protective security reports.
applicability: Supporting - NDIA must be able to produce portfolio evidence during Home Affairs assurance activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 04. Protective Security Reporting
description: The annual Cyber Security Survey is submitted to the Australian Signals Directorate.
applicability: Supporting - portfolio data should feed cyber survey inputs led by cyber security functions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
applicability: Direct - applies to prioritisation and risk acceptance for NDIA technology assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
applicability: Direct - applies to each material risk linked to applications, infrastructure, data assets and shared services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
applicability: Direct - applies where NDIA systems, data or services interoperate with other entities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
applicability: Direct - applies to all ICT procurement, renewal and sourcing decisions in the portfolio.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
applicability: Direct - applies to technology investments involving vendors, managed services, cloud or subcontractors.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
applicability: Direct - applies to service providers and contractors supporting NDIA ICT assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
applicability: Direct - applies to outsourced, cloud, software, infrastructure and support arrangements.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
applicability: Supporting - applies when NDIA consumes government-provided outsourced technology services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to ongoing portfolio assurance for supplier-delivered ICT services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to rationalisation, decommissioning, transition and contract exit decisions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
applicability: Direct - applies to vendor, product, managed service and hosting decisions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct - applies across the operational lifecycle of supplier-supported technology assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
applicability: Direct - applies to third-party technology vendors, services, platforms and integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Where exceptional circumstances prevent or affect an entity's capability to implement a PSPF requirement or standard, the Accountable Authority may vary application, for a limited period of time, consistent with the entity's risk tolerance.
applicability: Direct - applies where portfolio items cannot meet mandatory PSPF or security standards on schedule.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Decisions to vary implementation of a PSPF requirement or standard due to exceptional circumstances are documented in the entity's security plan.
applicability: Direct - applies to security exceptions arising from portfolio initiatives or legacy assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Decisions to implement an alternative mitigation measure that meets or exceeds a PSPF requirement or standard are reviewed and reported annually.
applicability: Direct - applies to compensating controls used for legacy, transitional or constrained ICT assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: A business continuity plan is developed, implemented and maintained to respond effectively and minimise the impacts of significant business disruptions to the entity's critical services and assets.
applicability: Direct - applies to NDIA critical applications, platforms, infrastructure, data stores and integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Plans for managing a broad range of emergencies are integrated within the business continuity plan.
applicability: Supporting - applies where ICT assets underpin emergency or continuity response capabilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
applicability: Direct - applies to data assets, information systems and applications processing official information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
applicability: Direct - applies to systems storing, processing, communicating or protecting official information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA handles caveated information in ICT systems or data holdings.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
applicability: Direct - applies to email, messaging, collaboration and workflow platforms used for government information exchange.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
applicability: Direct - applies to records, case management, content, data and knowledge management platforms.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
applicability: Direct - applies where NDIA systems categorise information access restrictions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 10. Information Holdings
description: Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
applicability: Direct - applies to all information holdings supported by NDIA applications, infrastructure and data platforms.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 10. Information Holdings
description: An auditable register is maintained for TOP SECRET information and accountable material.
applicability: Conditional - applies only if NDIA holds TOP SECRET information or accountable material in ICT-enabled holdings.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 11. Information Disposal
description: OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
applicability: Direct - applies to application retirement, data migration, storage decommissioning and archive decisions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 11. Information Disposal
description: Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA systems or media hold classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
applicability: Direct - applies to systems enabling access by external parties to classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: The Memorandum of Understanding between the Commonwealth, States and Territories is applied when sharing information with state and territory government agencies.
applicability: Conditional - applies to NDIA systems sharing information with state or territory agencies.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
applicability: Conditional - applies when portfolio initiatives share classified information or resources outside government.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Provisions are met concerning the security of people, information and resources contained in international agreements and arrangements to which Australia is a party.
applicability: Conditional - applies to ICT capabilities supporting international agreements or arrangements.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign entity is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies to systems or data flows involving foreign entities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where NDIA systems handle AUSTEO-caveated information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where NDIA systems handle AGAO-caveated information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Where an international agreement or arrangement is in place, security classified foreign entity information or resources are safeguarded in accordance with the provisions set out in the agreement or arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA systems hold or process foreign entity classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign non-government stakeholder is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies to initiatives sharing classified information or resources with foreign non-government stakeholders.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
applicability: Direct - central to NDIA application, infrastructure and data portfolio lifecycle management.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Direct - applies to investment cases, architecture decisions, remediation and rationalisation.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
applicability: Direct - applies to new systems, major upgrades, cloud services and platform changes.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
applicability: Direct - applies to portfolio intake, funding gates, major change and release governance.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
applicability: Direct - applies to systems processing, storing or communicating NDIA information and data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
applicability: Direct - core requirement for NDIA technology portfolio management.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
applicability: Direct - applies to change, upgrade, migration, rationalisation and threat-driven reassessment.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The TikTok application is prevented from being installed, and existing instances are removed, on government devices, unless a legitimate business reason exists.
applicability: Direct - applies to application portfolio governance and device/software standards.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The CSO or CISO approves any legitimate business reason for the use of the TikTok application on government devices and ensures specified mitigations are in place.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where a legitimate business reason for a prohibited application is proposed.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
