description: The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
applicability: Direct - applies to legacy applications, unsupported platforms, infrastructure and data technologies.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets and their components, classified as SECRET or below are stored in the appropriate Security Zone based on their aggregated security classification or business impact level.
applicability: Conditional - applies to technology assets classified SECRET or below or with relevant business impact levels.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets and their components classified as TOP SECRET are stored in suitable SCEC-endorsed racks or compartments within an accredited Security Zone Five area.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where NDIA operates or proposes TOP SECRET technology assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Outsourced facilities that house technology assets and their components with a catastrophic business impact level are certified by ASIO T4 physical security and accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
applicability: Direct - applies to all NDIA ICT-enabled projects and security assurance decisions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
applicability: Direct - applies to project risk registers, delivery partners and shared platform dependencies.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
applicability: Direct - applies where project decisions affect another entity, provider, scheme partner or shared service.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
applicability: Direct - applies to project sourcing, procurement strategies, statements of work and contract approvals.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
applicability: Direct - applies to all supplier engagements, including subcontracted delivery and managed services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
applicability: Direct - applies to supplier assurance checkpoints, design reviews, acceptance criteria and BAU handover.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
applicability: Direct - applies to supplier contracts, support models and delivery environments.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA consumes or assesses outsourced government ICT services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to project delivery, contract management planning and transition to operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to supplier contracts, transition-out plans and decommissioning activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
applicability: Direct - applies to technology procurement, maintenance, managed services and major supplier changes.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct - applies throughout project delivery and supplier contract lifecycle.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
applicability: Direct - applies to vendor selection, SaaS, cloud, integration partners and delivery tooling.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Where exceptional circumstances prevent or affect an entity's capability to implement a PSPF requirement or standard, the Accountable Authority may vary application, for a limited period of time, consistent with the entity's risk tolerance.
applicability: Conditional - applies when exceptional circumstances prevent or affect PSPF implementation in a project.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Decisions to vary implementation of a PSPF requirement or standard due to exceptional circumstances are documented in the entity's security plan.
applicability: Conditional - applies where a project variation, waiver or temporary exception is approved.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 08. Contingency Planning
description: Decisions to implement an alternative mitigation measure that meets or exceeds a PSPF requirement or standard are reviewed and reported annually.
applicability: Conditional - applies where projects use compensating or alternative mitigation measures.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
applicability: Direct - applies to project information, data sets, records, environments and system design.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
applicability: Direct - applies to project documentation, data migration, testing, environments and collaboration tooling.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
applicability: Conditional - applies where caveated information or special handling information is used, stored or shared.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
applicability: Direct - applies to project emails containing official, sensitive or classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
applicability: Conditional - applies where a system stores, processes or communicates security classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project systems use rights metadata or restriction categories to manage access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 10. Information Holdings
description: Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
applicability: Direct - applies to data architecture, operational readiness, controls design and handover.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 11. Information Disposal
description: OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
applicability: Direct - applies to data migration, test data, media, decommissioning and records disposal activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 11. Information Disposal
description: Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project activities handle or dispose of security classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
applicability: Direct - applies to suppliers, consultants, delivery partners and external users with access to NDIA information or systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: The Memorandum of Understanding between the Commonwealth, States and Territories is applied when sharing information with state and territory government agencies.
applicability: Conditional - applies where a project shares information with state or territory government agencies.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
applicability: Conditional - applies where security classified information is disclosed to vendors, partners or other non-government organisations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Provisions are met concerning the security of people, information and resources contained in international agreements and arrangements to which Australia is a party.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project scope includes international partners, offshore services or cross-border information sharing.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign entity is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies where a project proposes sharing classified information or resources with a foreign entity.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where AUSTEO caveated information or resources are in scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where AGAO caveated information or resources are in scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Where an international agreement or arrangement is in place, security classified foreign entity information or resources are safeguarded in accordance with the provisions set out in the agreement or arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies where foreign entity information or resources are stored, processed or communicated.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign non-government stakeholder is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies where a project proposes disclosure to foreign non-government stakeholders.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
applicability: Direct - applies to all new and changed NDIA technology systems and services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Direct - applies to solution architecture, control design, assurance and security acceptance.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
applicability: Direct - applies before go-live, pilot use, production data use or operational release.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
applicability: Direct - applies to new systems and material changes to existing systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
applicability: Direct - applies to classification, architecture, environment, hosting and authorisation decisions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
applicability: Direct - applies to go-live readiness, operational handover and system register maintenance.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
applicability: Direct - applies to change impact assessment and release governance.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The TikTok application is prevented from being installed, and existing instances are removed, on government devices, unless a legitimate business reason exists.
applicability: Direct - applies to project devices, managed endpoints, delivery tooling and application whitelisting.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The CSO or CISO approves any legitimate business reason for the use of the TikTok application on government devices and ensures specified mitigations are in place.
applicability: Conditional - applies only where a legitimate business reason for TikTok use is proposed.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project scope involves legacy, unsupported or hard-to-replace technology.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets and their components, classified as SECRET or below are stored in the appropriate Security Zone based on their aggregated security classification or business impact level.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project assets or components are classified SECRET or below or have aggregated impact.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets and their components classified as TOP SECRET are stored in suitable SCEC-endorsed racks or compartments within an accredited Security Zone Five area.
applicability: Conditional - rare; applies only to TOP SECRET technology assets or components.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Outsourced facilities that house technology assets and their components with a catastrophic business impact level are certified by ASIO T4 physical security and accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional - applies where outsourced facilities house catastrophic business impact technology assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the Information Security Manual.
applicability: Direct - applies to decommissioning, asset replacement, media sanitisation and disposal.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: A cyber security strategy and uplift plan is developed, implemented and maintained to manage the entity's cyber security risks in accordance with the ISM and the Guiding Principles to Embed a Zero Trust Culture.
applicability: Direct - applies to project alignment with NDIA cyber strategy, security roadmap and uplift priorities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Patch applications mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to applications introduced, configured, changed or supported by projects.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Patch operating systems mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to servers, endpoints, appliances and operating environments in project scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to user, privileged, remote, cloud and administrative access patterns.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to privileged accounts, administration tools, support models and service providers.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to project-managed endpoints, servers and application execution environments.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Restrict Microsoft Office macros mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies where Office documents, collaboration platforms or macro-enabled workflows are in scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: User application hardening mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to end-user computing, browser, PDF, web and collaboration components in scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Regular back-ups mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to data stores, applications, platforms and operational recovery requirements.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: The remaining mitigation strategies from the Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents are considered and, where required, implemented to achieve an acceptable level of residual risk for their entity.
applicability: Direct - applies through risk assessment and security control selection for all projects.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: A Protective Domain Name System service or other security mechanisms is used to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints.
applicability: Direct - applies to internet-connected systems, services, endpoints and cloud workloads.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project scope includes Cloud Service Providers or cloud-hosted services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Conditional - applies where IRAP-assessed services, cloud platforms or managed services are used.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Security classified or systems of government significance information and data is securely hosted using a Cloud Service Provider and Data Centre Provider that has been certified against the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
applicability: Conditional - applies where classified or systems of government significance information is hosted or processed.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: The Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel is used when procuring certified data centre space and services.
applicability: Conditional - applies where project scope includes procurement of certified data centre space or services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Internet-connected technology systems, and the data they process, store or communicate, are protected by a gateway in accordance with the ISM and the Gateways Policy.
applicability: Direct - applies to internet-connected systems and data flows delivered or changed by projects.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Gateways or Secure Service Edges that have completed an IRAP assessment (or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways) against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
applicability: Conditional - applies where projects introduce or materially change gateways or Secure Service Edge services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: A vulnerability disclosure program and supporting processes and procedures are established to receive, verify, resolve and report on vulnerabilities disclosed by both internal and external sources.
applicability: Direct - applies to public-facing, internet-connected or materially changed digital services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Protective security is integrated in the process of planning, selecting, designing and modifying entity facilities for the protection of people, information and resources.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies when a project creates, modifies or depends on a facility or secure work area.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: A facility security plan is developed for new facilities, facilities under construction or major refurbishments of existing facilities.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies to new facilities, construction or major refurbishment in project scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Decisions on entity facility locations are informed by considering the site selection factors for Australian Government facilities.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project scope includes selecting or relocating facilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: When designing or modifying facilities, the entity secures and controls access to facilities to meet the highest risk level to entity resources.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project scope designs or modifies facilities or secure areas.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Facilities are constructed in accordance with the applicable ASIO Technical Notes to protect against the highest risk level.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where facilities are constructed or modified to protect government information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 23. Physical Security Lifecycle
description: Facilities for Security Zones Two to Five that process, store or communicate security classified information and resources are constructed in accordance with the applicable sections of ASIO Technical Notes.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project facilities process, store or communicate classified information in Zones Two to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Security Zones One to Four are certified by the Certification Authority in accordance with the PSPF and applicable ASIO Technical Notes before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project deliverables rely on Security Zones One to Four.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Security Zone Five areas that contain TOP SECRET security classified information or aggregated information are certified by ASIO T4 before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional interface - rare; applies where a project uses Security Zone Five areas.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Security Zones One to Five are accredited by the Accreditation Authority before they are used operationally, on the basis that the required security controls are certified and the entity determines and accepts the residual risks.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project outcomes rely on Security Zones One to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 24. Security Zones
description: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility areas used to secure and access TOP SECRET systems and security classified compartmented information are accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
applicability: Conditional interface - rare; applies only to Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility areas.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to minimise or remove the risk of information and physical asset resources being made inoperable or inaccessible, or being accessed, used or removed without appropriate authorisation.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies to projects deploying or modifying physical technology assets or secure spaces.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to protect entity resources, commensurate with the assessed business impact level of their compromise, loss or damage.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project assets, locations or physical controls are in scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to minimise or remove the risk of harm to people.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project changes affect physical environments or people safety.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: The appropriate container, safe, vault, cabinet, secure room or strong rooms is used to protect entity information and resources based on the applicable Security Zone and business impact level.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where information or assets require physical containment.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Perimeter doors and hardware in areas that process, store or communicate security classified information or resources are constructed and secured in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project spaces process, store or communicate classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Access by authorised personnel, vehicles and equipment to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project deliverables are located in or access Security Zones One to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Access by visitors to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for access control for visitors.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where suppliers or visitors require access to Security Zones One to Five.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: The Accountable Authority or CSO approves ongoing (or regular) access to entity facilities for people who are not directly engaged by the entity or covered by the terms of a contract or agreement.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where vendors or third parties need ongoing or regular access to NDIA facilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Unauthorised access to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for security alarm systems.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where project facilities or secure zones require alarm controls.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Security guard arrangements in Security Zones One to Five are established in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for security guards.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where guard services are required for affected Security Zones or facilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Technical surveillance countermeasures for Security Zones One to Five are established in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Conditional interface - applies where TSCM is required for affected Security Zones or sensitive spaces.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: A Technology Asset Stocktake and Technology Security Risk Management Plan is created to identify and manage the entity's internet-facing systems or services to ensure continuous visibility and monitoring of the entity's resource and technology estate.
applicability: Direct - applies to internet-facing systems, services, APIs, domains and externally accessible technology assets.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: Approved post-quantum cryptographic encryption algorithms are used for newly procured cryptographic equipment and software in accordance with the ISM's guidelines for cryptography.
applicability: Conditional - applies to newly procured cryptographic equipment, software, protocols or services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Digital Infrastructure that processes, stores or communicates Australian Government security classified information is protected by a Gateway or Security Service Edge in accordance with the Australian Government Gateway Security Standard.
applicability: Conditional - applies where digital infrastructure processes, stores or communicates security classified information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Connect to the Australian Signals Directorate's Cyber Threat Intelligence Sharing platform.
applicability: Strategic/operational - applies to security platforms, SOC integrations and threat intelligence capabilities in project scope.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 15. Cyber Security Programs
description: Declared Systems of Government Significance are protected in accordance with the Australian Government Systems of Government Significance Standard.
applicability: Conditional - applies where the system or service is declared, or may be declared, a System of Government Significance.

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s15 - duty to govern the Commonwealth entity
description: The accountable authority must govern in a way that promotes proper use and management of public resources, achievement of entity purposes and financial sustainability.
applicability: NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity, so the PGPA Act applies to the NDIA accountable authority and officials.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013
type: Statutory governance, performance and accountability obligation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s16 - duty to establish risk oversight, risk management and internal control systems
description: The accountable authority must establish and maintain appropriate systems for risk oversight and management and internal control.
applicability: Directly relevant to all NDIA projects because projects introduce delivery, financial, privacy, cyber, fraud, dependency and operational risks.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013
type: Statutory governance, performance and accountability obligation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act ss25-29 - duties of officials
description: Officials must exercise care and diligence, act honestly, act in good faith and for proper purpose, not misuse position or information, and disclose material personal interests.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials involved in project decisions and informs expectations for contractor-facing governance.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013
type: Statutory governance, performance and accountability obligation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s35 and ss37-39 - corporate plan and performance statements
description: Entities must prepare corporate plans and annual performance statements that report on purposes and performance.
applicability: Applies to NDIA programs and projects that create capability, service, compliance or operational benefits.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013
type: Statutory governance, performance and accountability obligation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s41, s45 and s46 - records, audit committee and annual report
description: Entities must keep records, have audit committee arrangements and report annually.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA technology-enabled projects, especially projects subject to audit, committee oversight or annual reporting.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013
type: Statutory governance, performance and accountability obligation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s52 and s105B - spending commitments and procurement instruments
description: PGPA mechanisms regulate commitments of public resources and procurement-related instruments.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project procurement and contract management, alongside NDIA's own procurement policy and any applicable government directions.
source: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013
type: Statutory governance, performance and accountability obligation

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014 s10 - reasonable measures to prevent, detect and deal with fraud and corruption
description: Accountable authorities must take reasonable measures including risk assessments, control plans, periodic reviews, governance, records, prevention, detection, confidential reporting, investigation and incident reporting.
applicability: Mandatory for NDIA as a PGPA Act entity from the 2024 framework commencement.
source: PGPA Rule 2014 / Fraud and Corruption Rule
publisher: Department of Finance / Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre
type: Legislative instrument and mandatory fraud/corruption control obligation

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014 s10 - control plans and review
description: Fraud and corruption controls must be planned, implemented and periodically reviewed for effectiveness.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects with procurement, payments, participant data, identity, grants, provider interactions, system access or financial workflows.
source: PGPA Rule 2014 / Fraud and Corruption Rule
publisher: Department of Finance / Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre
type: Legislative instrument and mandatory fraud/corruption control obligation

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014 s10 - confidential reporting and response mechanisms
description: Entities must provide mechanisms for officials and others to report suspected fraud and corruption confidentially and must respond to incidents.
applicability: Mandatory for NDIA and must be visible to project teams and contractors.
source: PGPA Rule 2014 / Fraud and Corruption Rule
publisher: Department of Finance / Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre
type: Legislative instrument and mandatory fraud/corruption control obligation

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014 ss12-16C - disclosure of interests
description: The Rule contains requirements for officials to disclose interests in specified circumstances.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials participating in project governance, assurance, procurement, architecture and delivery decisions.
source: PGPA Rule 2014 / Fraud and Corruption Rule
publisher: Department of Finance / Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre
type: Legislative instrument and mandatory fraud/corruption control obligation

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - Policy and Guidance
description: The framework includes the Rule, Policy and Guidance; the Policy applies to non-corporate Commonwealth entities and corporate Commonwealth entities are encouraged to adopt it.
applicability: NDIA should apply the supporting Policy and Guidance where adopted by NDIA or where required by direction, funding conditions or assurance expectations.
source: PGPA Rule 2014 / Fraud and Corruption Rule
publisher: Department of Finance / Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre
type: Legislative instrument and mandatory fraud/corruption control obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act ss3-4 - objects and general principles
description: The Act sets the objects of the NDIS and principles guiding actions, including participation, choice and control for people with disability.
applicability: Directly applies to NDIA projects that affect participants, providers, staff, payments, planning, access, decisions or Scheme administration.
source: National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and NDIS Rules
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Department of Social Services
type: Statutory agency and service delivery obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act ss117-119 - establishment, functions and powers of the Agency
description: The Act establishes the NDIA and specifies its functions and powers.
applicability: Directly applies to all NDIA technology-enabled projects because they create or change capabilities used to perform NDIA functions.
source: National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and NDIS Rules
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Department of Social Services
type: Statutory agency and service delivery obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act Part 2 of Chapter 4, including s60 and ss62-67 - protection, use and disclosure of Agency information
description: The Act protects information held by the Agency and regulates use, disclosure and offences for unauthorised handling.
applicability: Directly applies to NDIA systems, data migration, reporting, analytics, portals, interfaces, support tooling, testing environments and supplier access.
source: National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and NDIS Rules
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Department of Social Services
type: Statutory agency and service delivery obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
description: Rules made for the NDIS Act support protection and authorised disclosure of information held by the Agency.
applicability: Applies where a project collects, uses, discloses, migrates, reports, tests with or gives access to Agency information.
source: National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and NDIS Rules
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Department of Social Services
type: Statutory agency and service delivery obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 provisions on participants, plans, payments, information-gathering and reviewable decisions
description: Operational provisions govern participant access, plans, payments, information requests, integrity and review processes.
applicability: Applies to projects affecting access, planning, payments, claims, provider interactions, notifications, evidence or decision records.
source: National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and NDIS Rules
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Department of Social Services
type: Statutory agency and service delivery obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act s15 and Schedule 1 - Australian Privacy Principles
description: APP entities must not do an act or practice that breaches an APP. The APPs regulate collection, use, disclosure, quality, security, access and correction of personal information.
applicability: Directly applies to NDIA as an Australian Government agency subject to the Privacy Act.
source: Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles and APP Code
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code s12 - Privacy Impact Assessment for high privacy risk projects
description: Agencies must conduct a PIA for all high privacy risk projects involving new or changed ways of handling personal information that are likely to have a significant impact on privacy.
applicability: Directly applies to NDIA projects assessed as high privacy risk; should be screened for every project.
source: Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles and APP Code
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code s15 - PIA register
description: Agencies must maintain and publish a register of PIAs completed for high privacy risk projects unless an exception applies.
applicability: Applies to NDIA high privacy risk projects subject to the Privacy Code.
source: Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles and APP Code
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act Part IIIC - Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
description: Agencies must assess and notify eligible data breaches that are likely to result in serious harm, subject to the Act.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project delivery and transition activities involving personal information.
source: Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles and APP Code
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act and APP contractual handling obligations
description: Agencies remain accountable for personal information handled by contracted service providers and must use appropriate safeguards and contractual arrangements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA suppliers and subcontractors that access or handle NDIA personal information.
source: Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles and APP Code
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives Information Management Standard - scope
description: The National Archives is the lead agency for Australian Government information management and the Standard applies to non-corporate and corporate Commonwealth entities, including outsourced information.
applicability: Directly applies to NDIA and information created or managed by NDIA staff, contractors and service providers.
source: Archives Act 1983 and Information Management Standard for Australian Government
type: Statutory obligation / mandatory information management standard

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Information Management Standard Principle 1 - systematic governance
description: Business information must be governed systematically with roles, controls and accountability.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA project workspaces and supplier-managed repositories containing Commonwealth records.
source: Archives Act 1983 and Information Management Standard for Australian Government
type: Statutory obligation / mandatory information management standard

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Information Management Standard Principle 2 - necessary business information is created
description: Agencies must create the business information needed to support decisions, rights, entitlements, accountability and continuity.
applicability: Applies to project business cases, gate packs, decision logs, architecture decisions, test records, benefits evidence and operational acceptance records.
source: Archives Act 1983 and Information Management Standard for Australian Government
type: Statutory obligation / mandatory information management standard

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Information Management Standard - information is findable, retrievable, trusted, complete and accurate
description: Business information should be findable, retrievable, trusted, complete, accurate and retained for as long as needed and no longer.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project and portfolio reporting evidence and supporting records.
source: Archives Act 1983 and Information Management Standard for Australian Government
type: Statutory obligation / mandatory information management standard

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Records authorities and disposal authorisations
description: Records authorities are legal instruments that authorise retention, destruction or transfer of records.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project closure, transition, decommissioning and supplier offboarding.
source: Archives Act 1983 and Information Management Standard for Australian Government
type: Statutory obligation / mandatory information management standard

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act ss11 and 11A - right of access to documents
description: The Act gives a legally enforceable right to access documents of an agency or official document of a Minister, subject to exemptions and conditions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project records, decision records, reports, vendor documents held by NDIA and operational material.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and Information Publication Scheme
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act Part II - Information Publication Scheme
description: Agencies must publish specified information and operational information, subject to exceptions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects that change public-facing services, operational guidance, forms, digital channels or participant/provider information.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and Information Publication Scheme
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act s6C - Commonwealth contracts and documents
description: The Act includes requirements relating to documents held by contractors in connection with Commonwealth contracts in specified circumstances.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project contracts and statements of work where suppliers create or hold project or service records.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and Information Publication Scheme
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: FOI Act decision and consultation provisions
description: The Act provides mechanisms for FOI decisions, reasons and consultation where documents affect third parties or exemptions may apply.
applicability: Applies to project records involving personal information, business information, security, Cabinet or internal deliberative matters.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and Information Publication Scheme
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Freedom of Information Act 1982
reference: OAIC FOI Guidelines issued under FOI Act s93A
description: Agencies and Ministers must have regard to the Information Commissioner's guidelines when performing FOI functions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA FOI handling and project teams supporting FOI searches or publication obligations.
source: Freedom of Information Act 1982 and Information Publication Scheme
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act s10 - APS Values
description: The APS Values require impartial, committed to service, accountable, respectful and ethical public administration.
applicability: NDIA is a PS Act body; APS employees working on NDIA projects must uphold the APS Values.
source: Public Service Act 1999, APS Values and APS Code of Conduct
type: Statutory APS conduct and integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act s13 - APS Code of Conduct
description: APS employees must behave honestly and with integrity, act with care and diligence, comply with laws and lawful directions, and avoid improper use of information or position.
applicability: Applies to NDIA APS employees and informs conduct expectations for mixed project teams and vendor governance.
source: Public Service Act 1999, APS Values and APS Code of Conduct
type: Statutory APS conduct and integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act ss12-15 - agency head obligations and breach processes
description: Agency heads must uphold and promote APS Values and Code of Conduct, and agencies must have processes for suspected breaches.
applicability: Applies to NDIA management of APS employee conduct in project settings.
source: Public Service Act 1999, APS Values and APS Code of Conduct
type: Statutory APS conduct and integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: APSC guidance on APS Values, Code of Conduct and Employment Principles
description: The APSC explains agency and employee responsibilities for upholding the values and Code and the consequences of breach.
applicability: Relevant to NDIA project onboarding, role descriptions, steering committees and assurance teams.
source: Public Service Act 1999, APS Values and APS Code of Conduct
type: Statutory APS conduct and integrity obligation

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Disability Discrimination Act ss5-6 - direct and indirect disability discrimination
description: The Act prohibits direct and indirect discrimination on the ground of disability.
applicability: Directly relevant to NDIA given its statutory purpose and user base, and applies to project design and implementation of services and systems.
publisher: Australian Human Rights Commission / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Disability Discrimination Act s24 and s29 - goods, services, facilities and Commonwealth programs
description: The Act prohibits discrimination in the provision of goods, services and facilities and in administration of Commonwealth laws and programs.
applicability: Applies to NDIA participant, provider, staff and public-facing technology-enabled change.
publisher: Australian Human Rights Commission / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Digital Inclusion Standard Criterion 4 - make it accessible
description: Government digital services should comply with disability discrimination law, the latest WCAG and the Australian Government Style Manual, and accessibility should be included in procurement and testing.
applicability: Applies to NDIA digital services that are subject to the Digital Experience Policy or where NDIA adopts the standard as its design baseline.
publisher: Australian Human Rights Commission / Federal Register of Legislation

name: Disability Discrimination Act 1992
reference: Disability Discrimination Act provisions on standards and action plans
description: The Act supports disability standards and action plans to reduce discrimination and improve accessibility.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects with participant, public or staff impacts and should align with NDIA accessibility and inclusion commitments.
publisher: Australian Human Rights Commission / Federal Register of Legislation

name: ICT Investment IOF
reference: DTA Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework - application and states
description: The IOF covers early planning to delivery and benefits, with states for strategic planning, prioritisation, contestability, assurance, sourcing and operations.
applicability: For corporate Commonwealth entities such as NDIA, application is conditional where specifically requested or otherwise triggered, but the framework is directly relevant to ICT investment governance.
source: Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework

name: ICT Investment IOF
reference: IOF strategic planning and prioritisation
description: Agencies plan digital investment and identify capability gaps, priorities and dependencies across the portfolio.
applicability: Applies to NDIA portfolio-level planning and to projects that depend on or change shared capabilities.
source: Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework

name: ICT Investment IOF
reference: IOF contestability
description: Contestability tests whether proposals are robust, value for money and aligned to whole-of-government requirements before government consideration.
applicability: Applies to NDIA proposals brought forward through government/DTA processes or internally adopted contestability arrangements.
source: Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework

name: ICT Investment IOF
reference: IOF assurance and conditions
description: The IOF establishes assurance expectations and monitors conditions, risks and outcomes across delivery.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects subject to DTA assurance, funding conditions or internal equivalent gates.
source: Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework

name: ICT Investment IOF
reference: IOF operations state
description: The operations state considers ongoing digital and ICT capability and performance beyond project delivery.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects that deliver or change operational ICT services.
source: Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework

name: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments
reference: DTA Assurance Framework - agencies must plan and implement assurance arrangements
description: The framework requires assurance arrangements for relevant investments and uses independent, objective assessments to support successful delivery.
applicability: Mandatory for in-scope non-corporate Commonwealth entity investments; for NDIA, applies when requested or adopted and should be used as a benchmark for major projects.
source: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments

name: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments
reference: DTA Assurance Framework Step 1 - investment tier
description: DTA confirms an investment tier based on risk, cost, complexity and significance.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects subject to DTA assurance or internal tiering aligned to DTA principles.
source: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments

name: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments
reference: DTA Assurance Framework Step 2 - assurance plan
description: Agencies develop assurance plans based on investment tier and requirements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects subject to DTA or NDIA assurance gates.
source: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments

name: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments
reference: Independent and objective assessment principle
description: Assurance should provide independent and objective assessment of whether investments are on track and risks are being managed.
applicability: Applies to major NDIA projects and any project with high delivery, security, privacy, financial or participant impact risk.
source: Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments

name: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook
reference: Digital Investment Plan Policy - agencies subject to IOF must have short, medium and long-term digital plans
description: The policy requires agencies subject to IOF to maintain digital investment plans across time horizons.
applicability: Applies to NDIA where IOF is triggered or adopted; highly relevant to NDIA portfolio planning and dependency management.
source: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook

name: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook
reference: Digital Investment Plan Policy - responsible officer
description: Agencies must designate a responsible officer for the Digital Investment Plan.
applicability: Applies to NDIA if subject to the policy and supports internal accountability even where not triggered.
source: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook

name: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook
reference: Digital Investment Plan Policy - proposals, projects and ongoing initiatives align to the DIP
description: Proposals, projects and ongoing digital initiatives assessed by DTA should align with the relevant DIP.
applicability: Applies to NDIA proposals subject to DTA assessment or adopted internal planning disciplines.
source: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook

name: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook
reference: Digital Investment Plan Policy - internally funded critical initiatives
description: DIPs should outline internally funded critical initiatives and align with strategic and corporate planning and enterprise architecture roadmaps.
applicability: Relevant to internally funded NDIA ICT projects even where a new policy proposal is not involved.
source: Digital Investment Plan Policy and Guidebook

name: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-Enabled Investments
reference: Benefits Management Policy - proposals define purpose, outcomes, measures and monitoring
description: Digital and ICT-enabled investment proposals are expected to define purpose, outcomes, performance measures and how improvements will be monitored and optimised.
applicability: Mandatory for in-scope investments and directly relevant to all NDIA technology-enabled projects seeking measurable service, compliance, cost, risk or productivity benefits.
source: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-enabled investments
type: Policy requirement for benefits identification, monitoring and realisation

name: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-Enabled Investments
reference: Benefits Management process - identify and analyse benefits
description: The process identifies benefit drivers, dependencies, baselines, benefit owners and expected outcomes.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects with participant, provider, operational, financial, compliance or risk-reduction outcomes.
source: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-enabled investments
type: Policy requirement for benefits identification, monitoring and realisation

name: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-Enabled Investments
reference: Benefits Management process - plan, monitor and realise
description: Benefits realisation plans are live artefacts that assign roles, responsibilities, dependencies and monitoring arrangements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project managers, sponsors, business owners and operational owners.
source: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-enabled investments
type: Policy requirement for benefits identification, monitoring and realisation

name: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-Enabled Investments
reference: Benefits Management process - review
description: Benefits are reviewed after implementation to test whether outcomes have been realised and to identify lessons or optimisation actions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects at closure, transition to operations and planned benefit review points.
source: Benefits Management Policy for Digital and ICT-enabled investments
type: Policy requirement for benefits identification, monitoring and realisation

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Experience Policy - mandated policy supported by four standards
description: The policy is supported by Digital Service Standard, Digital Inclusion Standard, Digital Access Standard and Digital Performance Standard.
applicability: Applies to services and investments subject to the policy/IOF. NDIA should apply it as a baseline for participant, provider and staff-facing services.
source: Digital Experience Policy and supporting standards
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Experience Policy - coverage of public-facing and staff-facing services
description: The policy covers specified new, replacement and existing digital services, including informational and transactional services where in scope.
applicability: Applies to NDIA portals, forms, websites, staff services, assisted digital channels and related service changes where triggered or adopted.
source: Digital Experience Policy and supporting standards
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard
description: The standard sets expectations for user-centred service design and delivery.
applicability: Applies to NDIA service changes in scope and should inform agile, waterfall, hybrid or scaled delivery approaches.
source: Digital Experience Policy and supporting standards
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Performance Standard
description: The performance standard supports monitoring of digital service performance.
applicability: Applies to in-scope NDIA digital services and internal policy adoption.
source: Digital Experience Policy and supporting standards
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Access Standard
description: The access standard addresses channels and access points for services.
applicability: Applies to NDIA public, participant, provider and staff services within scope.
source: Digital Experience Policy and supporting standards
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard
reference: Australian Government Architecture - review before investment, ICT capability development or digital procurement
description: Agencies should review AGA capabilities, policies, standards and design artefacts before investment, capability development or procurement.
applicability: Applies to all agencies when delivering digital outcomes; DTA tests alignment for new investments within IOF. For NDIA, use as architecture baseline and when triggered by IOF/DTA.
source: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard

name: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard
reference: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy - reuse wherever possible
description: The policy expects agencies to reuse existing capabilities wherever possible and avoid duplicating investment.
applicability: Mandatory for non-corporate Commonwealth entities; corporate Commonwealth entities are encouraged to apply. DTA uses it when assessing relevant proposals.
source: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard

name: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard
reference: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy - design and build for reuse
description: When new capability is developed, agencies should design and build it so it can be reused.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects developing platforms, integrations, APIs, data products, design patterns or shared services.
source: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard

name: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard
reference: AGA - consistent, interoperable and lower-risk digital outcomes
description: AGA aims to support consistent, interoperable, reusable and value-for-money government digital outcomes.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects integrating with internal or external systems, whole-of-government services, data platforms or shared identity capabilities.
source: Digital and ICT Reuse Policy and Reuse Standard

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM risk management framework - define, select, implement, assess, authorise and monitor
description: The ISM describes a cyber security framework for protecting IT and operational technology systems and a risk management framework for security controls.
applicability: Not a statute by itself, but mandatory where required by law, policy, contract, direction, PSPF, funding condition or NDIA security governance; should be the baseline for NDIA A&A.
source: Information Security Manual and Essential Eight Maturity Model
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate / Australian Cyber Security Centre
type: Cyber security standard and control framework

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ISM system boundary, security objectives and system security plan
description: The ISM requires definition of system boundaries and security objectives and documentation in system security plans.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects delivering new systems, major changes, integrations, cloud services or hosted services.
source: Information Security Manual and Essential Eight Maturity Model
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate / Australian Cyber Security Centre
type: Cyber security standard and control framework

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight mitigation strategies
description: The Essential Eight are baseline cyber mitigation strategies intended to make it harder for adversaries to compromise systems.
applicability: Applies to NDIA systems and suppliers where Essential Eight is required by NDIA security policy, PSPF, contracts or risk acceptance.
source: Information Security Manual and Essential Eight Maturity Model
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate / Australian Cyber Security Centre
type: Cyber security standard and control framework

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight Maturity Model
description: Entities identify a target maturity level, progressively implement controls, document approved exceptions and review them.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects that create or materially change systems in scope for Essential Eight assessment.
source: Information Security Manual and Essential Eight Maturity Model
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate / Australian Cyber Security Centre
type: Cyber security standard and control framework

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: PSPF Policy 10 amendment - Essential Eight requirement for NCEs
description: PSPF Policy 10 was amended to mandate Essential Eight requirements for non-corporate Commonwealth entities.
applicability: Applies to NDIA where PSPF/E8 requirements are adopted, directed, contractually required or used as internal security baseline.
source: Information Security Manual and Essential Eight Maturity Model
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate / Australian Cyber Security Centre
type: Cyber security standard and control framework

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF policy - covered systems and data
description: Sensitive government data, whole-of-government systems and PROTECTED systems must be hosted using certified services.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects procuring or extending hosting for sensitive government data, whole-of-government systems or PROTECTED systems.
source: Hosting Certification Framework and Whole-of-Government Hosting Strategy
type: Mandatory hosting and security policy for covered systems and data

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF requirements apply to new contracts and contract extensions
description: HCF requirements apply to new contracts and extensions for covered hosting services from the policy commencement arrangements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects and operational transitions involving hosting procurements, extensions or service changes.
source: Hosting Certification Framework and Whole-of-Government Hosting Strategy
type: Mandatory hosting and security policy for covered systems and data

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF supports PSPF and ISM objectives
description: The framework supports privacy, sovereignty and security objectives and assists government customers sourcing hosting services.
applicability: Applies to NDIA architecture and security reviews for hosted services and managed ICT environments.
source: Hosting Certification Framework and Whole-of-Government Hosting Strategy
type: Mandatory hosting and security policy for covered systems and data

name: Hosting Certification Framework (HCF) / Secure Cloud
reference: HCF certified providers and exceptions
description: The framework recognises certified providers and allows specified exemption pathways where certification is pending or not applicable.
applicability: Applies where a preferred hosting option is not certified or the project believes HCF does not apply.
source: Hosting Certification Framework and Whole-of-Government Hosting Strategy
type: Mandatory hosting and security policy for covered systems and data

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - applicability
description: The policy applies to non-corporate Commonwealth entities, with corporate Commonwealth entities encouraged to adopt, and takes effect from the stated date.
applicability: For NDIA, application is encouraged or required if adopted, directed, contractually required or attached to funding/assurance; HCF, privacy and security obligations can still be mandatory.
type: Policy requirement effective 1 July 2026 for non-corporate Commonwealth entities

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Policy requirement to prioritise cloud when modernising IT infrastructure
description: The policy states an expectation to prioritise cloud solutions in modernisation contexts, subject to appropriate assessment.
applicability: Applies to NDIA where the policy is adopted or as an internal architecture benchmark for modernisation projects.
type: Policy requirement effective 1 July 2026 for non-corporate Commonwealth entities

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Cloud security, privacy and hosting dependencies
description: Cloud use must be considered with related HCF, PSPF, ISM, privacy and records obligations.
applicability: Applies to NDIA cloud projects and SaaS procurements involving personal, sensitive or protected information.
type: Policy requirement effective 1 July 2026 for non-corporate Commonwealth entities

name: Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
reference: Cloud transition and exit management
description: Cloud adoption should be managed across the service lifecycle, including operational and exit considerations.
applicability: Relevant to NDIA cloud solutions, particularly long-lived SaaS, PaaS, IaaS and managed service arrangements.
type: Policy requirement effective 1 July 2026 for non-corporate Commonwealth entities

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs issued under PGPA Act s105B
description: The CPRs set rules for how officials procure goods and services for covered entities, including value for money, efficient, effective, economical and ethical procurement.
applicability: NDIA is a non-prescribed corporate Commonwealth entity, so CPRs may not directly bind NDIA in the same way as NCEs/prescribed CCEs; PGPA proper use and NDIA procurement policy still apply.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules issued under the PGPA Act
type: Mandatory procurement rules and PGPA procurement controls
