name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Value for money principle
description: Procurement decisions should consider whole-of-life value, risk, quality, fitness for purpose, supplier capability and relevant costs and benefits.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA technology procurement under NDIA procurement policy and PGPA stewardship expectations.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules issued under the PGPA Act
type: Mandatory procurement rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Ethical, accountable and transparent procurement expectations
description: Commonwealth procurement frameworks require ethical conduct, probity, records and accountable decisions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials and procurement participants; suppliers must meet contractual and probity obligations.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules issued under the PGPA Act
type: Mandatory procurement rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: NDIA procurement complaint guidance
description: NDIA states it is a non-prescribed corporate Commonwealth entity and selects suppliers based on overall value for money.
applicability: Directly relevant to NDIA procurement governance and complaint handling.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules issued under the PGPA Act
type: Mandatory procurement rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Supplier contract management and acceptance
description: Procurement outcomes require contract management, performance monitoring, deliverable acceptance and dispute/escalation mechanisms.
applicability: Applies to NDIA technology suppliers, system integrators, cloud providers, consultants and managed service providers.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules issued under the PGPA Act
type: Mandatory procurement rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Digital Sourcing policies, BuyICT and sourcing framework
reference: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy - contract limit
description: Covered digital sourcing contracts and work orders should not exceed $100 million whole-of-life value including extensions under the policy.
applicability: Mandatory for non-corporate Commonwealth entities; corporate Commonwealth entities are encouraged to apply or may be required through adoption/direction/funding conditions.
source: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy / Digital Sourcing Framework
type: Digital sourcing policy and framework guidance

name: Digital Sourcing policies, BuyICT and sourcing framework
reference: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy - initial term and extensions
description: Initial contract terms should not exceed three years and extension options should not exceed three years under the policy.
applicability: Relevant to NDIA digital procurements, renewals and work orders where adopted or triggered.
source: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy / Digital Sourcing Framework
type: Digital sourcing policy and framework guidance

name: Digital Sourcing policies, BuyICT and sourcing framework
reference: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy - review before extension
description: Extension options should only be exercised after reviewing contractor performance and deliverables.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects and services with renewal or extension decisions.
source: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy / Digital Sourcing Framework
type: Digital sourcing policy and framework guidance

name: Digital Sourcing policies, BuyICT and sourcing framework
reference: Digital Sourcing Framework principles
description: The framework supports competition, iteration, outcomes, reuse, SME participation, open standards, cloud and cyber risk management.
applicability: Non-mandatory guidance but relevant to NDIA technology-enabled projects and can be adopted internally.
source: Digital Sourcing Contract Limits and Reviews Policy / Digital Sourcing Framework
type: Digital sourcing policy and framework guidance

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI in Government Policy - accountable official and governance
description: The policy requires governance arrangements such as an accountable official for AI use and responsible adoption.
applicability: NDIA should apply where a project includes AI or automated decision support, and may be required if directed, adopted or attached to funding/assurance.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government and supporting standards
type: Mandatory AI governance policy and standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI in Government Policy - transparency statements
description: The policy includes transparency requirements for AI use in government.
applicability: Applies to NDIA AI use cases that interact with participants, providers, staff decisions, communications, triage, analytics or service operations.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government and supporting standards
type: Mandatory AI governance policy and standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI in Government Policy - AI use case impact assessment and register
description: The policy includes AI use case accountability, registers and impact assessment requirements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA AI-enabled projects and pilots, including generative AI and automated decision support.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government and supporting standards
type: Mandatory AI governance policy and standard

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI in Government Policy - staff training and responsible use
description: The policy includes requirements for staff capability and responsible use of AI systems.
applicability: Applies where NDIA staff use or operate AI-enabled capabilities introduced by a project.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government and supporting standards
type: Mandatory AI governance policy and standard

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act 2024 - accredited Digital ID services and AGDIS participation
description: The Act establishes accreditation, participation and oversight arrangements for Digital ID services.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects that provide, rely on, integrate with or participate in regulated Digital ID services or AGDIS.
source: Digital ID Act 2024 and Digital ID Rules 2024
publisher: Department of Finance / Digital ID Regulator

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act privacy and accessibility/inclusion obligations
description: The Act includes privacy and accessibility-related obligations for accredited and participating Digital ID services.
applicability: Applies to NDIA Digital ID use cases involving participants, nominees, providers, staff or representatives.
source: Digital ID Act 2024 and Digital ID Rules 2024
publisher: Department of Finance / Digital ID Regulator

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Rules 2024 - participation approvals, incidents and redress
description: Rules support participation approvals, reportable incidents, redress and operational requirements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects integrated with Digital ID systems or relying parties.
source: Digital ID Act 2024 and Digital ID Rules 2024
publisher: Department of Finance / Digital ID Regulator

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act - voluntary and inclusive system design principles
description: The Digital ID framework is intended to support secure, voluntary and inclusive identity verification.
applicability: Applies to NDIA digital service projects that propose Digital ID as an access path.
source: Digital ID Act 2024 and Digital ID Rules 2024
publisher: Department of Finance / Digital ID Regulator

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: Data Availability and Transparency Act - DATA Scheme authorisations
description: The Act authorises safe sharing of Australian Government data by data custodians with accredited users through specified mechanisms.
applicability: Applies to NDIA projects using the DATA Scheme or sharing government data with accredited users or service providers under the Act.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme - safe and responsible data sharing
description: The Scheme is intended to support sharing Australian Government data safely and responsibly while working with privacy law.
applicability: Applies to NDIA data sharing projects and must be reconciled with NDIS protected information and privacy requirements.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme data sharing agreements
description: DATA Scheme sharing is supported by data sharing agreements and governance arrangements.
applicability: Applies where NDIA is a data custodian, accredited user or participant in DATA Scheme sharing arrangements.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner

name: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
reference: DATA Scheme breach and responsibility provisions
description: The Act contains responsibilities and breach mechanisms for Scheme participants.
applicability: Applies to NDIA data sharing under the DATA Scheme, including service providers and operational teams.
source: Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme
publisher: Office of the National Data Commissioner

name: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral obligations
reference: NACC Act - corruption issues and corrupt conduct
description: The Act defines corrupt conduct and corruption issues and establishes the National Anti-Corruption Commission.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials and project-related conduct, including conduct involving contracted service providers where relevant.
source: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral guidance
type: Statutory integrity and mandatory referral obligation

name: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral obligations
reference: NACC mandatory referrals - agency heads and PID officers
description: Agency heads and PID officers must refer suspected serious or systemic corrupt conduct to the NACC as soon as reasonably practicable, unless the NACC is already aware.
applicability: Applies to NDIA Chief Executive/agency head arrangements and PID officers where threshold is met.
source: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral guidance
type: Statutory integrity and mandatory referral obligation

name: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral obligations
reference: NACC Act - staff members include contracted service providers in specified contexts
description: The Act can cover conduct by public officials and certain contracted service providers.
applicability: Applies to NDIA contract delivery, supplier personnel and subcontractors where the Act applies.
source: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral guidance
type: Statutory integrity and mandatory referral obligation

name: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral obligations
reference: NACC voluntary referral and information provision pathways
description: The Act permits referrals and information provision about corruption issues in specified circumstances.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials who identify integrity concerns during project delivery or assurance.
source: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 and mandatory referral guidance
type: Statutory integrity and mandatory referral obligation

name: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and Commonwealth Ombudsman agency guidance
reference: PID Act - public interest disclosures and disclosable conduct
description: The Act provides a framework for disclosures of disclosable conduct and protections for public officials.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials and, in relevant circumstances, contracted service providers and their officers.
source: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and PID agency guidance

name: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and Commonwealth Ombudsman agency guidance
reference: PID Act - protections and reprisal provisions
description: The Act includes protections for disclosers and provisions relating to reprisal action.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project environments, including mixed teams of officials and contractors.
source: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and PID agency guidance

name: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and Commonwealth Ombudsman agency guidance
reference: PID Act - principal officer, authorised officer and supervisor obligations
description: The Act sets obligations for principal officers, authorised officers, supervisors and public officials in handling disclosures.
applicability: Applies to NDIA supervisors, managers and project governance participants.
source: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and PID agency guidance

name: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and Commonwealth Ombudsman agency guidance
reference: Ombudsman agency guidance - contracted providers
description: The Ombudsman guidance notes that the PID framework can apply to contracted service providers and supports agency procedures, training and culture.
applicability: Applies to NDIA contracts and supplier onboarding where Commonwealth contracted service provider provisions apply.
source: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 and PID agency guidance

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: PGPA Act s16 and Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
description: The CRMP supports the PGPA Act requirement to establish appropriate risk oversight, management and internal controls.
applicability: PGPA s16 directly applies to NDIA. CRMP is directly binding on NCEs and should be applied by NDIA where adopted or as better practice.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy supporting PGPA Act section 16

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - risk embedded in decision-making
description: The policy promotes risk management as part of governance, planning, delivery and decision-making.
applicability: Relevant to all NDIA technology-enabled projects and portfolio decisions.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy supporting PGPA Act section 16

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - shared and emerging risks
description: The policy encourages entities to manage risks that cut across organisational boundaries and evolve over time.
applicability: Applies to NDIA portfolio reporting and dependency management.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy supporting PGPA Act section 16

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Risk controls, treatment and monitoring
description: Effective risk management requires controls, treatments, accountable owners and monitoring.
applicability: Applies to NDIA project delivery, transition and operations handover.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy supporting PGPA Act section 16

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security Act Part 2 - security standards for smart devices
description: The Act provides for mandatory security standards for relevant connectable products, supported by Rules.
applicability: Applies if NDIA procures, supplies, pilots or integrates products that fall within the relevant connectable product regime or requires supplier compliance evidence.
source: Cyber Security Act 2024 and subordinate cyber security rules

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security Act Part 3 and Rules - ransomware payment reporting
description: The Act and Rules establish reporting obligations for ransomware or cyber extortion payments for covered entities and prescribed information.
applicability: Applicability to NDIA must be confirmed by legal/security advice for the specific incident and entity context; suppliers may have direct obligations.
source: Cyber Security Act 2024 and subordinate cyber security rules

name: Cyber Security Act 2024 and Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
reference: Cyber Security Act Part 4 - significant cyber security incident coordination and limited use
description: Impacted entities may voluntarily provide information to the National Cyber Security Coordinator, with limited-use protections in the Act.
applicability: Relevant to NDIA security incident response and project transition arrangements, especially for significant incidents.
source: Cyber Security Act 2024 and subordinate cyber security rules

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

description: The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must assess insider threat risk to participant data, scheme integrity, fraud controls, staff and ICT systems, and assign accountable treatment owners.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

description: Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA relies on contractors, labour hire, managed service providers and ICT suppliers whose access can affect participant information and scheme operations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 07. Countering Foreign Interference and Espionage

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
applicability: Directly applicable for OFFICIAL and sensitive NDIA information; conditional for classified or caveated material. The same handling discipline supports protection of participant and scheme information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
applicability: Directly applicable for OFFICIAL and sensitive NDIA information; conditional for classified or caveated material. The same handling discipline supports protection of participant and scheme information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
applicability: Directly applicable for OFFICIAL and sensitive NDIA information; conditional for classified or caveated material. The same handling discipline supports protection of participant and scheme information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Accountable material is handled in accordance with any special handling requirements imposed by the originator and security caveat owner.
applicability: Directly applicable for OFFICIAL and sensitive NDIA information; conditional for classified or caveated material. The same handling discipline supports protection of participant and scheme information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Security classified discussions and dissemination of security classified information are only conducted in approved locations.
applicability: Directly applicable for OFFICIAL and sensitive NDIA information; conditional for classified or caveated material. The same handling discipline supports protection of participant and scheme information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 10. Information Holdings
description: Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA holds high-value participant, provider, fraud, compliance and workforce information that requires proportional ICT and insider threat controls.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
applicability: Conditional for security classified information; also relevant to NDIA because external access to sensitive participant or scheme information must be limited to authorised, need-to-know users.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
applicability: Conditional for security classified information; relevant as a mandatory control model for NDIA information-sharing agreements with external organisations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Provisions are met concerning the security of people, information and resources contained in international agreements and arrangements to which Australia is a party.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA participates in international agreements or arrangements involving protected information, people or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign entity is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies when NDIA shares Australian Government security classified information or resources with a foreign entity.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA handles AUSTEO-caveated information; the policy should prohibit unauthorised disclosure by insiders.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA handles AGAO-caveated information; the policy should reinforce access and citizenship restrictions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Where an international agreement or arrangement is in place, security classified foreign entity information or resources are safeguarded in accordance with the provisions set out in the agreement or arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA receives foreign entity classified information or resources under an agreement or arrangement.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign non-government stakeholder is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA shares classified information or resources with foreign non-government stakeholders.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA ICT systems must be designed, changed, monitored and retired with controls that prevent and detect insider misuse or compromise.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA ICT systems must be designed, changed, monitored and retired with controls that prevent and detect insider misuse or compromise.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

applicability: Directly applicable - authentication, privileged-access restrictions and application control reduce malicious, negligent and compromised-user activity in NDIA ICT systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - authentication, privileged-access restrictions and application control reduce malicious, negligent and compromised-user activity in NDIA ICT systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Directly applicable - authentication, privileged-access restrictions and application control reduce malicious, negligent and compromised-user activity in NDIA ICT systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

description: The eligibility and suitability of personnel who have access to Australian Government people and resources is ensured.
applicability: Directly applicable - all personnel and contractors accessing NDIA resources should be screened before being trusted with participant information or scheme systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: The pre-employment screening identity check is conducted for all personnel, to verify identity to at least Level 3 (High) of Assurance of the National Identity Proofing Guidelines.
applicability: Directly applicable - all personnel and contractors accessing NDIA resources should be screened before being trusted with participant information or scheme systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: Biographic information in identity documents is verified to ensure the information matches the original record.
applicability: Directly applicable - all personnel and contractors accessing NDIA resources should be screened before being trusted with participant information or scheme systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: The pre-employment screening eligibility check is conducted for all personnel, to confirm their eligibility to work in Australia and for the Australian Government.
applicability: Directly applicable - all personnel and contractors accessing NDIA resources should be screened before being trusted with participant information or scheme systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025

description: The entity obtains assurance of each person's suitability to access Australian Government resources during pre-employment screening.
applicability: Directly applicable - all personnel and contractors accessing NDIA resources should be screened before being trusted with participant information or scheme systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Prior to granting temporary access to security classified information or resources, pre-employment checks are completed.
applicability: Conditional for temporary classified access; relevant to NDIA when personnel require temporary access while checks or clearances are underway.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A risk assessment determines whether a person is granted temporary access to security classified information or resources.
applicability: Conditional for temporary classified access; relevant whenever NDIA considers time-bound access to sensitive or classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Temporary access to security classified information, resources and activities is supervised.
applicability: Conditional for temporary classified access; supports NDIA supervision and monitoring of any temporary privileged or sensitive access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Short-term temporary access to security classified information, resources and activities is limited to the period in which an application for a security clearance is being processed, or up to a total combined maximum of three months in a 12-month period.
applicability: Conditional for temporary classified access; relevant where NDIA grants short-term access while a clearance application is processed.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: The Authorised Vetting Agency confirms that the completed security clearance pack has been received, and that no initial concerns have been identified, before short-term temporary access is changed to provisional temporary access.
applicability: Conditional for temporary classified access; applies where NDIA changes short-term access to provisional temporary access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Temporary access to classified caveated information, resources or activities is not granted, other than in exceptional circumstances, and only with the approval of the caveat controlling authority.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA handles classified caveated information; access must remain exceptional and controlled.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Prior to granting temporary access, the entity obtains an undertaking from the person to protect the security classified information, resources and activities they will access.
applicability: Conditional for temporary classified access; relevant to NDIA undertakings for protecting sensitive or classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Prior to granting temporary access, the entity obtains agreement from any other entity (or third party) whose security classified information, resources and activities will be accessed by the person during the temporary access period.
applicability: Conditional for temporary access to another entity's or third party's classified information, resources or activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Access to official information is facilitated for entity personnel and other relevant stakeholders.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only given to entity personnel with a need-to-know that information.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel requiring ongoing access to security classified information or resources are security cleared to the appropriate level.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel requiring access to caveated information meet any clearance and suitability requirements imposed by the originator and caveat controlling authority.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A unique user identification, authentication and authorisation practice is implemented on each occasion where system access is granted, to manage access to systems holding security classified information.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions by the CSO to allow personnel to work in another government entity's facilities in Australia.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: An agreement is in place to manage the security risks associated with personnel working in another government entity's facilities in Australia.
applicability: Directly applicable for official information and ICT systems; conditional for classified or caveated access. Access decisions must reflect need-to-know and insider threat risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Approval for remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems in international locations is only granted if approved by the Australian Signals Directorate.
applicability: Conditional - applies only if NDIA requires international remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions to allow personnel to work remotely in international locations.
applicability: Directly relevant to international remote work and conditional for classified systems; applies to protecting NDIA information outside Australia.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel are not granted approval to work remotely in locations where Australian Government information or resources are exposed to extrajudicial directions from a foreign government that conflict with Australian law, unless operationally required.
applicability: Directly relevant to international remote work where foreign law or directions could expose NDIA information or ICT resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The AGSVA or the TOP SECRET-Privileged Access Vetting Authority is used to conduct security vetting.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The gaining sponsoring entity establishes new clearance conditions before assuming sponsorship of an existing security clearance that is subject to clearance conditions.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The gaining sponsoring entity undertakes the exceptional business requirement and risk assessment provisions prior to requesting transfer of sponsorship of an existing security clearance that is subject to an eligibility waiver.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: Positions that require a security clearance are identified and the level of clearance required is documented.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: Each person working in an identified position has a valid security clearance issued by the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: Australian citizenship is confirmed and pre-employment screening is completed before the entity seeks a security clearance for a person.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity establishes an exceptional business need and conducts a risk assessment before a citizenship eligibility waiver is considered for a non-Australian citizen.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Accountable Authority (or the CSO if delegated) approves a citizenship eligibility waiver and maintains a record of all citizenship eligibility waivers approved.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity establishes an exceptional business need and conducts a risk assessment before a checkable background eligibility waiver is considered.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity's Accountable Authority (or the CSO if delegated) approves checkable background eligibility waivers and maintains a record of all such waivers approved.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors, manages or requires security clearances; it informs trusted access decisions for sensitive roles and classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
