description: The Sponsoring Entity actively assesses, monitors and manages the ongoing suitability of personnel.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity monitors and manages compliance with any conditional security clearance requirements and reports any non-compliance to the Authorised Vetting Agency.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity monitors and manages compliance with security clearance maintenance obligations for the clearance holders they sponsor.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity shares relevant information of concern, where appropriate.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity conducts an annual security check with all security cleared personnel.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity reviews eligibility waivers at least annually, before revalidation of a security clearance, and prior to any proposed position transfer.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity monitors, assesses and manages personnel with TOP SECRET-Privileged access security clearances in accordance with the TOP SECRET-Privileged Access Standard.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA sponsors or manages TOP SECRET-Privileged Access clearance holders.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity shares relevant information of security concern, where appropriate with the Authorised Vetting Agency.
applicability: Conditional for clearance holders and directly relevant to high-risk ICT roles. NDIA should use ongoing suitability signals, support and escalation to manage insider risk.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: Negative Vetting 2 and higher clearance holders receive appropriate departmental travel briefings when undertaking international personal and work travel.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA has NV2 or higher clearance holders undertaking personal or work travel overseas.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: The CSO, CISO (or other relevant security practitioner) is advised prior to separation or transfer of any proposed cessation of employment resulting from misconduct or other adverse reasons.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must manage insider risk during transfers, adverse separations and departures by removing access, preserving evidence and reminding personnel of obligations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: Separating personnel are informed of any ongoing security obligations under the Commonwealth Criminal Code and other relevant legislation.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must manage insider risk during transfers, adverse separations and departures by removing access, preserving evidence and reminding personnel of obligations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: Separating personnel transferring to another Australian Government entity — the entity, when requested, provides the receiving entity with relevant security information.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must manage insider risk during transfers, adverse separations and departures by removing access, preserving evidence and reminding personnel of obligations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: Separating personnel transferring to another Australian Government entity — the entity reports any security concerns to ASIO.
applicability: Conditional - applies when a separating person transfers to another Australian Government entity and security concerns require ASIO reporting.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: A risk assessment is completed to identify any security implications in situations where it is not possible to undertake the required separation procedures.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must manage insider risk during transfers, adverse separations and departures by removing access, preserving evidence and reminding personnel of obligations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: Separating personnel have their access to Australian Government resources withdrawn upon separation or transfer from the entity.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must manage insider risk during transfers, adverse separations and departures by removing access, preserving evidence and reminding personnel of obligations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: The Sponsoring Entity advises the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency of the separation of a clearance holder, including any relevant circumstances.
applicability: Directly applicable - NDIA must manage insider risk during transfers, adverse separations and departures by removing access, preserving evidence and reminding personnel of obligations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to minimise or remove the risk of information and physical asset resources being made inoperable or inaccessible, or being accessed, used or removed without appropriate authorisation.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Physical security measures are implemented to protect entity resources, commensurate with the assessed business impact level of their compromise, loss or damage.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Access by authorised personnel, vehicles and equipment to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Access by visitors to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for access control for visitors.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: The Accountable Authority or CSO approves ongoing (or regular) access to entity facilities for people who are not directly engaged by the entity or covered by the terms of a contract or agreement.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Unauthorised access to Security Zones One to Five is controlled in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for security alarm systems.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
description: Security guard arrangements in Security Zones One to Five are established in accordance with the physical security measures and controls for security guards.
applicability: Supporting control - applies to NDIA workplaces, secure areas, devices, records and visitor arrangements that could enable unauthorised ICT or information access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity ensures clearance subjects with an eligibility waiver or where a waiver is being considered, are not given temporary or provisional access to security classified information or resources until the security vetting process is complete.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA considers or manages eligibility waivers for clearance subjects and temporary or provisional access.

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - cyber security governance, risk management and system authorisation guidance
description: Systems should be governed, risk-assessed and authorised with accountable ownership and documented security controls.
applicability: Applies to NDIA business systems, identity platforms, monitoring tools, cloud services and administrative environments.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - Guidelines for Access Control
description: Access should be granted only to authorised users, restricted to business need and regularly reviewed.
applicability: Applies to NDIA role-based access, participant information, scheme integrity data, HR systems and privileged administration.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - Guidelines for Privileged Access
description: Privileged access should be restricted, attributable, controlled and subject to additional safeguards.
applicability: Applies to NDIA system administrators, database administrators, cloud administrators, security administrators and vendor support accounts.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - Guidelines for Event Logging and Monitoring
description: Security-relevant events should be logged, protected, monitored and retained to support detection and investigation.
applicability: Applies to NDIA identity, endpoint, email, cloud, database, DLP, VPN and privileged-access logs.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - Guidelines for System Monitoring
description: System monitoring should be proportionate, authorised and aligned to security objectives.
applicability: Applies to NDIA UEBA, DLP, endpoint monitoring, email security, cloud activity monitoring and privileged-session monitoring.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - Guidelines for Cyber Security Incidents
description: Entities should prepare for, detect, analyse, contain, eradicate and recover from cyber security incidents.
applicability: Applies to NDIA insider incident playbooks, triage categories, evidence preservation and post-incident improvement.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: ASD ISM - data transfer, removable media and data spill controls
description: Data movement and spills should be controlled, logged and remediated according to information sensitivity.
applicability: Applies to NDIA email, cloud storage, collaboration platforms, removable media, printing and downloads from core systems.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Application Control
description: Only approved applications should execute on systems at the required maturity level.
applicability: Applies to NDIA endpoints, servers, privileged workstations and administrative tooling.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Patch Applications and Patch Operating Systems
description: Applications and operating systems should be patched within required timeframes based on risk and maturity level.
applicability: Applies to NDIA managed devices, servers, network appliances, cloud-hosted systems and security monitoring infrastructure.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Configure Microsoft Office Macro Settings and User Application Hardening
description: User applications should be hardened to reduce common attack paths and unsafe content execution.
applicability: Applies to NDIA productivity platforms, browsers, PDF readers and collaboration tools.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Restrict Administrative Privileges
description: Administrative privileges should be limited, controlled and reviewed.
applicability: Applies to NDIA administrators, elevated service accounts, developers, database administrators and break-glass users.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Multi-factor Authentication
description: Multi-factor authentication should protect privileged access, remote access and important systems.
applicability: Applies to NDIA remote access, privileged accounts, cloud applications, security tools and sensitive data repositories.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Regular Backups
description: Important data and systems should be backed up and recoverable.
applicability: Applies to NDIA core systems, logs, case management records, security evidence and configuration data.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: PSPF Reqs 99-107 and Essential Eight Maturity Model - minimum maturity expectations
description: Entities must meet required Essential Eight maturity expectations and apply other mitigations as required by PSPF.
applicability: Applies to NDIA enterprise cyber controls and systems that store protected Agency information or enable privileged access.
type: Cyber security control baseline / maturity guidance

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act ss 10-12 - Commonwealth entities, corporate Commonwealth entities and accountable authorities
description: The PGPA Act defines Commonwealth entities and accountable authority responsibilities.
applicability: NDIA is a body corporate under the NDIS Act and the PGPA Act applies to the Agency as a corporate Commonwealth entity.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s15 - duty to govern the Commonwealth entity
description: The accountable authority must govern the entity in a way that promotes proper use and management of public resources and achievement of purposes.
applicability: Applies to the NDIA Board/CEO oversight of insider-risk controls across ICT, people, information and contractors.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s16 - duty to establish and maintain systems relating to risk and control
description: The accountable authority must establish and maintain systems for risk oversight, risk management and internal control.
applicability: Applies to NDIA risk registers, control libraries, monitoring, access reviews, DLP controls, incident processes and assurance.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s17 - duty to encourage cooperation with others
description: The accountable authority must encourage officials to cooperate with others to achieve common objectives.
applicability: Applies to the NDIA cross-functional insider-threat working group and incident coordination model.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s18 - requirements imposed on others in relation to public resources
description: Accountable authorities must consider requirements imposed on others in relation to public resources.
applicability: Applies to NDIA vendors, contractors, consultants and managed service providers using NDIA systems or information.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s19 - duty to keep the responsible Minister and Finance Minister informed
description: The accountable authority must keep relevant Ministers informed about significant issues affecting the entity.
applicability: Applies to NDIA escalation thresholds for material insider incidents, data breaches, corruption, fraud or operational disruption.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act ss 25-29 - officials' duties: care, diligence, honesty, proper purpose, use of position, use of information and conflicts
description: Officials must act with care and diligence, honestly, in good faith and for proper purpose; must not misuse position or information and must disclose interests.
applicability: Applies to NDIA officials, including staff and members of the accountable authority; equivalent obligations should be imposed contractually on contractors.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10 - preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and corruption
description: Accountable authorities must take all reasonable measures to prevent, detect and respond to fraud and corruption.
applicability: Applies to NDIA insider-risk scenarios involving participant payments, provider relationships, scheme integrity data and privileged system access.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act ss 37-41 - performance records, measurement, annual performance statements, accounts and records
description: Entities must keep records needed to measure performance and manage accounts and records.
applicability: Applies to NDIA insider-risk metrics, case records, evidence, control assurance and governance reporting.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s45 - audit committee for Commonwealth entities
description: Commonwealth entities must have an audit committee that can provide oversight of risk, controls and performance.
applicability: Applies to NDIA risk/audit committee reporting on insider-threat risk, control maturity and significant control failures.
publisher: Department of Finance / Federal Register of Legislation

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(a) - fraud and corruption risk assessments
description: Entities must conduct fraud and corruption risk assessments.
applicability: Applies to NDIA risks involving participant payments, provider collusion, unauthorised browsing, data theft, manipulation of records and privileged access misuse.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(b) - fraud and corruption control plans
description: Entities must prepare and implement plans to control fraud and corruption risks.
applicability: Applies to NDIA entity-level and business-unit fraud control planning.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(c) - prevention, detection and response controls
description: Entities must have appropriate prevention, detection and response arrangements.
applicability: Applies to NDIA Security Operations, fraud control, business integrity teams and system owners.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(d) - governance, capability and awareness
description: Entities must establish governance, roles, responsibilities and awareness arrangements for fraud and corruption control.
applicability: Applies to NDIA executives, managers, staff, contractors, security teams and HR/legal/privacy partners.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(e) - confidential reporting of suspected fraud and corruption
description: Entities must provide ways for officials and others to report suspected fraud and corruption confidentially.
applicability: Applies to NDIA internal reporting, whistleblower/PID channels, manager escalation, security reporting and anonymous reporting where available.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(f) - investigations and other responses
description: Entities must have arrangements to investigate or otherwise respond to fraud and corruption incidents.
applicability: Applies to NDIA insider incident triage, fraud investigation, cyber incident response and misconduct processes.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10(g) - recording and reporting fraud and corruption incidents
description: Entities must record and report fraud and corruption incidents as required.
applicability: Applies to NDIA case management, incident registers, reporting to oversight bodies and governance dashboards.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - prevention and detection focus
description: The framework establishes a whole-of-government approach to preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and corruption.
applicability: Applies to NDIA scenarios where a trusted insider may exploit access for financial gain, conflict of interest, collusion or unauthorised disclosure.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024 - data and analytics as detection support
description: Entities should use available information and analytics to improve fraud and corruption detection.
applicability: Applies to NDIA data from access logs, claims systems, provider interactions, DLP tools, identity systems and HR/security case data.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: Fraud and Corruption Rule and external referral obligations
description: Suspected criminal, corrupt or serious matters may require referral to AFP, NACC or other appropriate bodies.
applicability: Applies to NDIA suspected bribery, collusion, unauthorised disclosure for benefit, system manipulation and high-impact misuse.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10 - reasonable measures for contractors and third parties
description: Fraud and corruption controls must address risks from officials and external parties where relevant.
applicability: Applies to NDIA outsourced ICT, contractors, labour-hire staff, consultants and providers with privileged or data access.

name: PGPA Rule 2014
reference: PGPA Rule 2014, s10 - response and remediation
description: Entities must respond to incidents and improve controls after fraud and corruption events.
applicability: Applies to NDIA control remediation after insider events, including access model changes, DLP tuning, process redesign and staff training.

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(1)-(3) - integrity, care, diligence and respect
description: APS employees must behave honestly, with integrity, care and diligence, and treat everyone with respect and courtesy.
applicability: Applies to NDIA APS employees and should be reflected in equivalent contractor conduct obligations.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(4)-(5) - comply with laws and lawful directions
description: APS employees must comply with Australian laws and lawful and reasonable directions.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA staff using NDIA systems, information and devices.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(6) - maintain confidentiality
description: APS employees must maintain appropriate confidentiality about dealings with Ministers, ministerial staff and other employees.
applicability: Applies to NDIA staff handling insider investigations, HR matters, security cases and confidential government information.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(7)-(8) - proper use of Commonwealth resources and avoid improper advantage
description: APS employees must use Commonwealth resources properly and must not use duties, status, power or authority to gain or seek a benefit.
applicability: Applies to NDIA systems, devices, accounts, privileged tools, data exports and communication platforms.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(10)-(11) - no false or misleading information and no improper use of inside information, duties, status, power or authority
description: APS employees must not knowingly give false or misleading information and must not improperly use inside information or powers.
applicability: Applies to NDIA case records, investigation interviews, access requests, declarations, conflicts and audit responses.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(12) - disclose and take reasonable steps to avoid conflicts of interest
description: APS employees must disclose and take reasonable steps to avoid conflicts of interest.
applicability: Applies to NDIA employees with provider, participant, vendor, family, financial or outside-employment interests relevant to their access or decisions.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s13(13) - uphold APS Values, Employment Principles and integrity and good reputation of employee's agency and the APS
description: APS employees must uphold the integrity and good reputation of the APS and their agency.
applicability: Applies to NDIA workforce conduct online, in systems, during investigations and after separation where obligations continue.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, ss14-15 - sanctions and procedures for breaches of the Code of Conduct
description: Agencies must have procedures for determining Code breaches and may impose sanctions for breaches.
applicability: Applies to NDIA HR-led misconduct processes linked to insider events, including suspension, reassignment, sanctions and termination.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: Public Service Act 1999, s10A - APS Employment Principles
description: Employment decisions must be merit-based and workplaces must be free from discrimination and patronage.
applicability: Applies to NDIA onboarding, ongoing suitability, role-change reassessment and separation handling.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Public Service Act 1999 Cth
reference: NDIS Act 2013, s169 - NDIA staff engaged under the Public Service Act
description: The NDIA's staff must be persons engaged under the Public Service Act; the CEO and staff constitute a Statutory Agency.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA staff; contractor obligations should mirror relevant APS conduct, confidentiality and ICT requirements through contracts.
publisher: Australian Public Service Commission / Federal Register of Legislation
type: APS Code of Conduct and employment integrity obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act 1988, s14 and APP 1 - open and transparent management of personal information
description: APP entities must manage personal information in an open and transparent way and have appropriate practices, procedures and privacy policies.
applicability: Applies to NDIA collection and use of monitoring logs, HR indicators, investigation records and user activity data.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 3 - collection of solicited personal information
description: Personal information may only be collected where reasonably necessary for, or directly related to, an agency's functions or activities.
applicability: Applies to NDIA UEBA, DLP, endpoint logs, email metadata, access logs, HR/security indicators and investigation records.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 5 - notification of collection
description: Individuals must be notified of certain matters when personal information is collected, where required.
applicability: Applies to NDIA logon banners, acceptable use terms, privacy notices, onboarding materials and monitoring notices.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 6 - use or disclosure of personal information
description: Personal information must generally be used or disclosed only for the purpose collected, or a permitted secondary purpose.
applicability: Applies to sharing monitoring data with HR, Legal, Security, Welfare, law enforcement, OAIC or other bodies.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 10 - quality of personal information
description: APP entities must take reasonable steps to ensure personal information used or disclosed is accurate, up to date and complete.
applicability: Applies to NDIA analytics, alert triage, investigation records and HR decisions based on monitoring outputs.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11 - security of personal information
description: APP entities must protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.
applicability: Applies to NDIA insider case files, UEBA datasets, HR indicators, DLP alerts, interview notes and evidence stores.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 12 and APP 13 - access to and correction of personal information
description: Individuals have rights to access and request correction of personal information, subject to applicable exceptions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA privacy requests involving monitoring records, investigation records and staff information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act 1988, Part IIIC - Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
description: Eligible data breaches likely to result in serious harm must be notified to affected individuals and the OAIC.
applicability: Applies to NDIA insider incidents involving participant, provider, employee or other personal information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act 1988 - sensitive information protections
description: Sensitive information requires careful handling and higher protection where collected or used.
applicability: Applies to NDIA participant data, access logs, case notes, provider information and employee welfare information.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: Privacy Act 1988 and APP Guidelines - privacy by design and risk management
description: Privacy risks should be considered in the design of systems, projects and information-handling practices.
applicability: Applies to NDIA procurement, configuration and rollout of monitoring and insider analytics tools.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 6 and APP 11 - disclosure and security of investigation data
description: Investigation information must be disclosed only when permitted and protected from unauthorised access.
applicability: Applies to NDIA Security, HR, Legal, Privacy, Welfare and business managers handling insider cases.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11 - destruction or de-identification when information is no longer needed, subject to Commonwealth records obligations
description: Personal information should be destroyed or de-identified when no longer needed unless retention is required by law or records obligations.
applicability: Applies to NDIA monitoring logs, UEBA data, DLP alerts, case files and investigation evidence.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner / Federal Register of Legislation
type: Privacy and personal information handling obligation

name: Privacy Code
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code - privacy officer and senior privacy champion
description: Agencies must assign privacy governance roles, including privacy officer functions and senior-level privacy leadership.
applicability: Applies to NDIA Privacy function participation in insider-threat governance and case escalation.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
type: Mandatory Australian Government agency privacy governance obligation

name: Privacy Code
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code - privacy management plan
description: Agencies must maintain a plan for managing privacy obligations and improving privacy maturity.
applicability: Applies to NDIA monitoring, HR/security case records, DLP programs, UEBA implementation and privacy assurance.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
type: Mandatory Australian Government agency privacy governance obligation

name: Privacy Code
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code - privacy impact assessments for high privacy risk projects
description: Agencies must conduct privacy impact assessments for projects that may have a high privacy impact.
applicability: Applies to NDIA new or materially changed monitoring, analytics, DLP, insider-case management or privileged-session recording solutions.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
type: Mandatory Australian Government agency privacy governance obligation

name: Privacy Code
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code - privacy training and awareness
description: Agencies must provide appropriate privacy education and awareness to staff.
applicability: Applies to NDIA staff, managers, privileged users, investigators and security analysts.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
type: Mandatory Australian Government agency privacy governance obligation

name: Privacy Code
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code - privacy governance in procurements and projects
description: Agencies must embed privacy in projects, procurements and information-handling practices.
applicability: Applies to NDIA procurement of security tooling, managed services, analytics platforms and case management solutions.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
type: Mandatory Australian Government agency privacy governance obligation

name: Privacy Code
reference: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code - records of PIAs and privacy assurance
description: Agencies must maintain evidence of privacy assessments and governance decisions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA privacy records, governance papers, PIA registers and control assurance evidence.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
type: Mandatory Australian Government agency privacy governance obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, s60 - protection of information held by the Agency
description: Information held by the Agency is protected and may be used or disclosed only as authorised.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA ICT systems and personnel handling protected Agency information.
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Federal Register of Legislation
type: NDIA governance and protected Agency information obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, s62 - offence: unauthorised use or disclosure of protected Agency information
description: Unauthorised making of a record, use or disclosure of protected Agency information can be a criminal offence.
applicability: Applies to NDIA employees, former employees, contractors and others with access to protected Agency information.
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Federal Register of Legislation
type: NDIA governance and protected Agency information obligation

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013, s63 - offence: soliciting disclosure of protected Agency information
description: It is an offence to solicit disclosure of protected Agency information in unauthorised circumstances.
applicability: Applies to NDIA staff and contractors who are approached by providers, participants, acquaintances or external actors seeking protected information.
publisher: National Disability Insurance Agency / Federal Register of Legislation
type: NDIA governance and protected Agency information obligation

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
applicability: Supporting - applies to identity risk acceptance, IAM exceptions and control design for all NDIA digital identity populations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
applicability: Supporting - applies to identity lifecycle risks, privileged access risks, federated access and third-party access administration.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 05. Security Risk Management
description: The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
applicability: Supporting - applies where NDIA shares identity services, authentication decisions, federated access or identity risk information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
applicability: Direct - applies to contractors, partners, providers, managed service providers and any third party with NDIA system access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
applicability: Direct - applies to all outsourced services, contractors, subcontractors, partners and providers requiring NDIA digital access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
applicability: Direct - applies to third parties and subcontractors with NDIA system access or IAM responsibilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
applicability: Direct - applies to third parties operating, administering or using NDIA identities, credentials or access control services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to ongoing assurance of supplier access, subcontractor access and provider/partner integrations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to all third-party and contractor identities and service integrations at contract completion or termination.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
applicability: Supporting - applies to third-party services that administer identities, provide identity tooling or access NDIA systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
applicability: Direct - applies to all third-party access arrangements over the contract lifecycle.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 06. Third Party Risk Management
description: Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
applicability: Direct - applies to identity platforms, integration services, managed service providers, partners and provider access services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
applicability: Direct - applies to role-based and attribute-based access design, entitlement approval and access review.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
applicability: Direct - applies to access to OFFICIAL and security classified information through NDIA systems.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA systems hold or provide access to caveated information.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 09. Classifications and Caveats
description: Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
applicability: Supporting - applies to systems capable of metadata-driven access control or recordkeeping integration.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
applicability: Conditional - applies to people outside NDIA who require digital access to security classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA enables access for persons or organisations outside government to classified resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA systems handle AUSTEO information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 12. Information Sharing
description: Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
applicability: Conditional - applies where NDIA systems handle AGAO information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
description: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
applicability: Direct - applies to identity stores, directories, IAM tooling, federation, authentication, authorisation and logging services.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to privileged, remote, workforce and high-risk external access; participant and provider authentication as risk assessed.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 14. Cyber Security Strategies
description: Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
applicability: Direct - applies to all administrative, privileged, break-glass and service administration accounts.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: The eligibility and suitability of personnel who have access to Australian Government people and resources is ensured.
applicability: Direct for staff and contractors; conditional for partners/providers with NDIA resource access; not applicable to participants as personnel screening.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: The pre-employment screening identity check is conducted for all personnel, to verify identity to at least Level 3 (High) of Assurance of the National Identity Proofing Guidelines.
applicability: Direct for staff, contractors and personnel identities; informs assurance levels for provider and participant identities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: Biographic information in identity documents is verified to ensure the information matches the original record.
applicability: Direct for personnel onboarding; risk-based for provider, partner and participant identities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: The pre-employment screening eligibility check is conducted for all personnel, to confirm their eligibility to work in Australia and for the Australian Government.
applicability: Direct for staff and contractors; not applicable to participant accounts except where separate legislative eligibility rules apply.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 16. Pre-Employment Eligibility
description: The entity obtains assurance of each person's suitability to access Australian Government resources during pre-employment screening.
applicability: Direct for workforce personnel; conditional for providers and partners with government resource access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Prior to granting temporary access to security classified information or resources, pre-employment checks are completed.
applicability: Conditional - applies to temporary access to security classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A risk assessment determines whether a person is granted temporary access to security classified information or resources.
applicability: Conditional - applies to temporary access to security classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Temporary access to security classified information, resources and activities is supervised.
applicability: Conditional - applies to temporary access to security classified information, resources or activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Short-term temporary access to security classified information, resources and activities is limited to the period in which an application for a security clearance is being processed, or up to a total combined maximum of three months in a 12-month period.
applicability: Conditional - applies to short-term temporary access while security clearance processing is underway.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: The Authorised Vetting Agency confirms that the completed security clearance pack has been received, and that no initial concerns have been identified, before short-term temporary access is changed to provisional temporary access.
applicability: Conditional - applies to provisional temporary access to security classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Temporary access to classified caveated information, resources or activities is not granted, other than in exceptional circumstances, and only with the approval of the caveat controlling authority.
applicability: Conditional - applies to temporary access to classified caveated information, resources or activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Prior to granting temporary access, the entity obtains an undertaking from the person to protect the security classified information, resources and activities they will access.
applicability: Conditional - applies before temporary access to security classified information, resources or activities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Prior to granting temporary access, the entity obtains agreement from any other entity (or third party) whose security classified information, resources and activities will be accessed by the person during the temporary access period.
applicability: Conditional - applies where temporary access includes classified information, resources or activities owned by another entity or third party.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Access to official information is facilitated for entity personnel and other relevant stakeholders.
applicability: Direct - applies to entity personnel and relevant stakeholders including contractors, partners and providers.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
applicability: Direct - core IAM requirement for all NDIA digital identity populations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Access to security classified information or resources is only given to entity personnel with a need-to-know that information.
applicability: Conditional - applies to security classified information and resources; the least-privilege principle applies more broadly.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel requiring ongoing access to security classified information or resources are security cleared to the appropriate level.
applicability: Conditional - applies to ongoing access to security classified information or resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel requiring access to caveated information meet any clearance and suitability requirements imposed by the originator and caveat controlling authority.
applicability: Conditional - applies to access to caveated information and resources.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A unique user identification, authentication and authorisation practice is implemented on each occasion where system access is granted, to manage access to systems holding security classified information.
applicability: Direct - core requirement for NDIA IAM across staff, contractors, partners, providers and participants.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions by the CSO to allow personnel to work in another government entity's facilities in Australia.
applicability: Supporting - applies where IAM enables access from another government entity's Australian facilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: An agreement is in place to manage the security risks associated with personnel working in another government entity's facilities in Australia.
applicability: Supporting - applies where personnel access NDIA systems while working in another government entity's Australian facilities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Approval for remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems in international locations is only granted if approved by the Australian Signals Directorate.
applicability: Conditional - applies only to TOP SECRET international remote access scenarios.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions to allow personnel to work remotely in international locations.
applicability: Supporting - applies to international remote access requests; conditional where classified information is involved.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 17. Access to Resources
description: Personnel are not granted approval to work remotely in locations where Australian Government information or resources are exposed to extrajudicial directions from a foreign government that conflict with Australian law, unless operationally required.
applicability: Supporting - applies to international remote access and high-risk locations.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The AGSVA or the TOP SECRET-Privileged Access Vetting Authority is used to conduct security vetting.
applicability: Conditional - applies where access requires a security clearance.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The gaining sponsoring entity establishes new clearance conditions before assuming sponsorship of an existing security clearance that is subject to clearance conditions.
applicability: Conditional - applies when NDIA assumes sponsorship of a clearance subject to conditions.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The gaining sponsoring entity undertakes the exceptional business requirement and risk assessment provisions prior to requesting transfer of sponsorship of an existing security clearance that is subject to an eligibility waiver.
applicability: Conditional - applies when NDIA seeks transfer of a clearance subject to an eligibility waiver.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: Positions that require a security clearance are identified and the level of clearance required is documented.
applicability: Direct for workforce role design; conditional for systems or roles requiring classified access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: Each person working in an identified position has a valid security clearance issued by the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency.
applicability: Conditional - applies to personnel in roles requiring a valid security clearance.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: Australian citizenship is confirmed and pre-employment screening is completed before the entity seeks a security clearance for a person.
applicability: Supporting - applies to personnel onboarding prior to clearance-dependent access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity establishes an exceptional business need and conducts a risk assessment before a citizenship eligibility waiver is considered for a non-Australian citizen.
applicability: Conditional - applies to non-Australian citizens needing clearance-dependent access.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Accountable Authority (or the CSO if delegated) approves a citizenship eligibility waiver and maintains a record of all citizenship eligibility waivers approved.
applicability: Conditional - applies where clearance-dependent access relies on a citizenship eligibility waiver.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity establishes an exceptional business need and conducts a risk assessment before a checkable background eligibility waiver is considered.
applicability: Conditional - applies where clearance-dependent access may rely on a checkable background eligibility waiver.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity's Accountable Authority (or the CSO if delegated) approves checkable background eligibility waivers and maintains a record of all such waivers approved.
applicability: Conditional - applies where clearance-dependent access relies on a checkable background eligibility waiver.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity actively assesses, monitors and manages the ongoing suitability of personnel.
applicability: Direct for workforce and third-party access; conditional for participant or provider accounts through risk-based monitoring.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity monitors and manages compliance with any conditional security clearance requirements and reports any non-compliance to the Authorised Vetting Agency.
applicability: Conditional - applies to personnel with conditional clearance requirements.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 21. Maintenance and Ongoing Assessment
description: The Sponsoring Entity monitors and manages compliance with security clearance maintenance obligations for the clearance holders they sponsor.
applicability: Conditional - applies to clearance holders sponsored by NDIA.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: The CSO, CISO (or other relevant security practitioner) is advised prior to separation or transfer of any proposed cessation of employment resulting from misconduct or other adverse reasons.
applicability: Direct - applies to staff, contractors and third-party workforce identities.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: A risk assessment is completed to identify any security implications in situations where it is not possible to undertake the required separation procedures.
applicability: Direct - applies to exceptional separation, abandonment, urgent termination or inaccessible-account scenarios.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: Separating personnel have their access to Australian Government resources withdrawn upon separation or transfer from the entity.
applicability: Direct - core joiner/mover/leaver requirement for workforce and third-party identities; applies to providers and participants when access relationship changes.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 22. Separation
description: The Sponsoring Entity advises the relevant Authorised Vetting Agency of the separation of a clearance holder, including any relevant circumstances.
applicability: Conditional - applies to clearance holders sponsored by NDIA.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2025
reference: 18. Security Clearances
description: The Sponsoring Entity ensures clearance subjects with an eligibility waiver or where a waiver is being considered, are not given temporary or provisional access to security classified information or resources until the security vetting process is complete.
applicability: Conditional - applies where an eligibility waiver is being considered or has been granted.

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM Cyber Security Principle PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
description: Robust and secure identity, credential and access management establishes, maintains and controls access and supports detection of misuse.
applicability: Applies to every NDIA user, customer, provider, partner, service account, device, certificate and AI agent identity.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM Cyber Security Principle PRO-12 - Least privilege
description: Access privileges should be limited to the minimum required to perform authorised functions.
applicability: Applies across workforce, participant support, provider functions, administrators, service accounts and AI agents.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - Guidelines for system hardening: authentication hardening
description: Systems should harden authentication methods, disable insecure authentication and apply MFA where required.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA internet-facing, remote access, privileged, workforce, provider and high-risk participant-facing services.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - Guidelines for system management: privileged operating environments
description: Privileged administration should use controlled environments and separate administrative paths.
applicability: Applies to directory administrators, identity platform administrators, cloud administrators, CIAM administrators and security operations roles.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ASD guidance - Restricting administrative privileges
description: Administrative privileges should be restricted, controlled, reviewed and removed when not required.
applicability: Applies to NDIA administrators and third-party administrators for identity, cloud, application, database and network platforms.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - Event logging and monitoring controls
description: Security-relevant events should be logged, protected, monitored and retained to support detection and investigation.
applicability: Applies to identity providers, directories, PAM, federation gateways, CIAM, application authorization and non-human identities.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - Guidelines for software development: authentication and authorization
description: Software should implement secure authentication, authorization and session handling requirements from design through operation.
applicability: Applies to participant portals, provider portals, APIs, mobile apps, integration gateways and AI tool interfaces.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - Cryptography and certificate management controls
description: Cryptographic keys, certificates and protocols should be approved, protected and managed through their lifecycle.
applicability: Applies to SSO signing certificates, TLS certificates, mTLS credentials, API keys, service credentials and device identities.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - System administration and service account management
description: Privileged accounts, shared accounts and service accounts should be controlled and attributable.
applicability: Applies to service accounts, automation accounts, bots, devices, workloads and AI agents.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Information Security Manual (ISM)
reference: ISM - Security risk management and control assessment
description: Controls should be selected, implemented and assessed based on the system threat model, classification and risk environment.
applicability: Applies to NDIA identity control waivers, legacy systems, accessibility exceptions and partner federation exceptions.
source: Australian Government Information Security Manual controls and guidance
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Multi-factor authentication
description: MFA maturity levels define where MFA must be used, including privileged, remote, third-party and important system access.
applicability: Applies to NDIA workforce, administrators, providers, partners and high-risk customer or nominee access pathways.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Restrict administrative privileges
description: Administrative privileges must be limited, controlled, reviewed and removed when no longer required.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA and supplier administrators with elevated access to identity platforms, applications, infrastructure or data.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Patch applications
description: Applications must be patched or mitigated within timeframes based on risk and exploitability.
applicability: Applies to identity provider software, CIAM, PAM, federation proxies, application authentication libraries and agent runtimes.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Patch operating systems
description: Operating systems must be patched within maturity-model timeframes.
applicability: Applies to servers, endpoints, privileged access workstations, virtual appliances and identity infrastructure.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Application control
description: Application control prevents unapproved executables, scripts and installers from running.
applicability: Applies to privileged workstations, identity servers, PAM infrastructure and automation hosts.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - User application hardening
description: User-facing applications should disable risky features and reduce exploit paths.
applicability: Applies to workforce endpoints used for identity administration, support, participant management and provider administration.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Regular backups
description: Backups must be protected and recoverable to restore systems after compromise or loss.
applicability: Applies to identity directories, CIAM tenant configuration, federation metadata, PAM vaults, policy stores and audit configurations.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Essential Eight Maturity Model
reference: Essential Eight - Assessment process
description: Entities should assess maturity consistently and retain evidence of implementation and exceptions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA control self-assessments, supplier assurance and cyber uplift reporting.
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate (Australian Cyber Security Centre)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 1 - Open and transparent management of personal information
description: Entities must manage personal information in an open and transparent way, including policies, practices and privacy governance.
applicability: Applies to CIAM, workforce directories, provider identity, nominee access, identity proofing, logs and AI identity services.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 2 - Anonymity and pseudonymity
description: Individuals must have the option of not identifying themselves, or using a pseudonym, unless an exception applies.
applicability: Applies to enquiry, information, feedback and low-risk digital interactions; not to functions requiring identity verification or protected information access.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 3 - Collection of solicited personal information
description: Personal information must only be collected where reasonably necessary for the entity's functions or activities.
applicability: Applies to participants, nominees, providers, staff, contractors and partner identities.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 5 - Notification of collection
description: Individuals must be notified about collection, purpose, usual disclosures and consequences of non-collection.
applicability: Applies to online and assisted identity proofing, provider registration access, workforce onboarding and support channels.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 6 - Use or disclosure of personal information
description: Personal information must generally be used or disclosed only for the primary purpose of collection unless an exception applies.
applicability: Applies to identity data shared with Digital ID, DVS/FVS, service providers, partners, monitoring tools and AI systems.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 8 - Cross-border disclosure of personal information
description: Before disclosing personal information overseas, entities must take reasonable steps to ensure appropriate privacy protections unless an exception applies.
applicability: Applies to SaaS identity platforms, outsourced support, fraud detection services, logs and AI identity services hosted offshore.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 9 - Adoption, use or disclosure of government related identifiers
description: Government related identifiers must not be adopted, used or disclosed inappropriately.
applicability: Applies to participant, nominee and provider identity identifiers and matching processes.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 10 - Quality of personal information
