description: Entities must take reasonable steps to ensure personal information is accurate, up-to-date and complete.
applicability: Applies to participant details, nominee authority, provider relationships, workforce attributes and access roles.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11.1 - Security of personal information
description: Entities must take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.
applicability: Applies to all identity data, identity evidence, credentials, sessions, logs and authorization records.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 11.2 - Destruction or de-identification
description: Personal information must be destroyed or de-identified when no longer needed, unless retention is required or authorised by law.
applicability: Applies to CIAM proofing records, workforce records, nominee authority evidence, provider identity evidence and identity logs.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
reference: APP 12 and APP 13 - Access and correction
description: Individuals have rights to access and correct personal information, subject to exceptions.
applicability: Applies to identity profile data, contact details, representative authority, provider contacts and workforce attributes.
source: Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy governance requirements
description: Agencies must have privacy governance arrangements, including privacy leadership, roles and accountability.
applicability: Applies to NDIA identity product owners, privacy officers, security owners and program executives.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy management plan
description: Agencies must maintain a privacy management plan and integrate privacy into business practices.
applicability: Applies to CIAM, workforce identity, provider identity, Digital ID integration, AI identity and access governance.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy Impact Assessments for high privacy risk projects
description: Agencies must conduct PIAs for high privacy risk projects and maintain related governance.
applicability: Applies before major identity platform changes, new proofing methods, nominee access models, provider federation and AI access automation.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy training and awareness
description: Agencies must take steps to ensure staff understand their privacy obligations.
applicability: Applies to helpdesk, access administrators, security operations, developers, product owners and supplier personnel.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy by design
description: Agencies are expected to embed privacy into systems, projects and procurement.
applicability: Applies to identity architecture, account identifiers, federation claims, token content, logs, analytics and AI identity decisions.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Register and review of PIAs
description: Agencies should maintain records of PIAs and risk treatment decisions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA identity governance boards and assurance packs.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - High privacy risk project definition
description: Projects that involve new or changed ways of handling personal information and are likely to have significant privacy impacts require particular governance attention.
applicability: Applies to new identity platforms, new proofing methods, biometrics, large-scale access analytics and AI-driven access workflows.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy Officer
description: Agencies must have privacy officer arrangements to support privacy management.
applicability: Applies to NDIA identity governance forums and project approval gates.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy Champion
description: Agencies must have senior privacy leadership to promote a privacy culture.
applicability: Applies to cross-agency and enterprise identity decisions.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Privacy Code
reference: Privacy Code - Privacy capability
description: Agencies should build capability through training, guidance and integration into processes.
applicability: Applies to help desk, identity administrators, customer support, fraud, security and service teams.
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: NDB scheme - Eligible data breach
description: An eligible data breach occurs when personal information is lost, accessed or disclosed without authorisation and serious harm is likely.
applicability: Applies to breaches affecting participant, nominee, provider, workforce or identity evidence data handled by NDIA or suppliers.
source: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: NDB scheme - Assessment of suspected breach
description: Entities must assess suspected eligible data breaches and decide whether notification is required.
applicability: Applies to account takeover, credential stuffing, MFA bypass, unauthorised access grants, token leakage and supplier identity breaches.
source: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: NDB scheme - Notify affected individuals and OAIC
description: Where an eligible data breach occurs, affected individuals and the OAIC must be notified in accordance with the scheme.
applicability: Applies to NDIA notification decisions, communications, support channels and remediation actions.
source: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: NDB scheme - Remedial action
description: Effective remedial action can prevent a breach from becoming notifiable if it removes the likelihood of serious harm.
applicability: Applies to compromised accounts, incorrect entitlements, exposed keys, breached service accounts and leaked identity evidence.
source: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: NDB scheme - Supplier and third-party breaches
description: Entities remain responsible for managing notification obligations where service providers handle personal information.
applicability: Applies to contracted identity providers, cloud services, support vendors, verification services and federated partners.
source: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme
reference: NDB scheme - Post-incident improvement
description: Entities should review incidents and improve controls to prevent recurrence.
applicability: Applies after any identity or access incident, whether or not notifiable.
source: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988
publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act 2013 Part 2 Division 1 - Information held by Agency
description: The Act contains specific protections for information held by the Agency, including protected Agency information.
applicability: Applies directly to NDIA participant, nominee, provider and worker access to NDIS information.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act s 60 - Protection of information held by Agency
description: The Act protects information held by the Agency and frames how it may be handled.
applicability: Applies to all systems and users handling participant, nominee, provider, plan and payment information.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act s 62 - Unauthorised use or disclosure
description: Unauthorised use or disclosure of protected Agency information is an offence subject to statutory exceptions.
applicability: Applies to NDIA staff, contractors, secondees, service providers and any person with system access.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act ss 63-64 - Soliciting or offering protected information
description: The Act prohibits soliciting or offering protected information except as authorised.
applicability: Applies to privileged users, contact centre users, support workers, providers and partner users with data access.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act s 66 and related rules - Disclosure by CEO or delegate
description: Disclosure of protected information may occur only through authorised statutory pathways and rules.
applicability: Applies to information sharing through portals, APIs, data exchanges and delegated access arrangements.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS protected information guidance
description: NDIS guidance identifies sensitive categories such as legal name, nominee details, date of birth, disability evidence, supports and bank information.
applicability: Applies to participant and nominee profiles, contact centre identity verification, portal access and support workflows.

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act - Provider and registered provider functions
description: The Act and associated rules govern provider registration and interactions with NDIS functions.
applicability: Applies to provider portal users, partner access, support coordinators and organisation administrators.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS Act 2013
reference: NDIS Act - Evidence and accountability
description: The statutory scheme requires accountable decisions and lawful information handling.
applicability: Applies to entitlement approvals, access reviews, audit logs and support actions.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: NDIS Act Part 5 - Nominees
description: The Act provides for participant nominees, including plan nominees and correspondence nominees.
applicability: Applies to participant portals, nominee access, assisted digital channels and contact centre verification.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: Nominees Rules - Appointment and authority
description: The rules address whether a nominee should be appointed and the scope of nominee arrangements.
applicability: Applies to plan nominees, correspondence nominees and any delegated online access for representatives.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: Nominees Rules - Duties of nominees
description: Nominees have duties related to participant interests and wishes.
applicability: Applies to what nominees can view, change, approve or submit in participant services.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: Nominees Rules - Cancellation or suspension
description: Nominee appointments can be cancelled or suspended.
applicability: Applies to access provisioning, revocation, periodic validation and real-time authority checks.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: Nominees Rules - Correspondence nominee
description: A correspondence nominee may receive notices and correspondence for a participant.
applicability: Applies to notifications, document access, contact details and communication preferences.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: Nominees Rules - Plan nominee
description: A plan nominee may act in relation to preparation, review or implementation of a participant's plan within the appointment scope.
applicability: Applies to plan viewing, plan changes, service bookings, claims and consent flows.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: NDIS (Protection and Disclosure of Information) Rules 2013
reference: Nominee identity proofing
description: Nominee status relies on both verifying the nominee person and verifying their authority relationship.
applicability: Applies to new nominee onboarding, account recovery and high-risk changes.
source: NDIS Act 2013 and NDIS Rules instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA)

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act 2024 - Framework for regulated Digital ID services
description: The Act establishes principles, governance and oversight for entities providing or relying on Digital ID services.
applicability: Applies if NDIA relies on AGDIS, myID, RAM, accredited identity service providers or identity exchange providers.
source: Australian Government Digital ID System guidance
publisher: Department of Finance / Australian Government Digital ID System
type: Digital ID legislative and accreditation obligation

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Act 2024 - Voluntary, secure, convenient and inclusive identity verification
description: The Act aims to provide voluntary, secure, convenient and inclusive ways to verify identity online.
applicability: Applies to participant and nominee onboarding, account recovery and provider representative access.
source: Australian Government Digital ID System guidance
publisher: Department of Finance / Australian Government Digital ID System
type: Digital ID legislative and accreditation obligation

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Rules 2024
description: The Rules support operation, participation and obligations in the Digital ID system.
applicability: Applies to NDIA service owners integrating with AGDIS, identity exchange providers or accredited services.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / Department of Finance

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Accreditation Rules 2024 - accreditation obligations
description: Accreditation rules set requirements for entities seeking accreditation and ongoing compliance for Digital ID services.
applicability: Applies to selection and oversight of Digital ID identity providers, attribute providers and exchanges.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / Department of Finance

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Accreditation Rules - Identity proofing levels
description: Accreditation requirements define identity proofing levels and minimum requirements for binding proofing levels to Digital IDs.
applicability: Applies to participant account creation, nominee identity, high-risk recovery, staff proofing and provider principal authority proofing.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / Department of Finance

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID Accreditation Data Standards - Authentication levels
description: The standards define authentication levels and related technical data concepts.
applicability: Applies to login assurance for participants, nominees, providers, administrators and high-risk functions.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / Department of Finance

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Digital ID (AGDIS) Data Standards 2024 - SAML data flows and relying party audit identifiers
description: AGDIS data standards define data flows, including SAML use and relying-party transaction audit identifiers.
applicability: Applies to NDIA AGDIS relying-party integrations and audit logging.
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / Department of Finance

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: AGDIS and Relationship Authorisation Manager (RAM)
description: AGDIS includes RAM, enabling people to use Digital ID to act on behalf of a business for participating government services.
applicability: Applies to provider organisation administrators, principal authorities, agents and business representatives.
source: Australian Government Digital ID System architecture guidance

name: Digital ID Act 2024
reference: Trusted Digital Identity Framework (TDIF) transition
description: TDIF provided the predecessor trusted identity rules and informed Digital ID rules and data standards.
applicability: Applies where legacy TDIF assurance language exists in NDIA policies, contracts or system designs.
publisher: Department of Finance / Australian Government Digital ID System

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
description: The Act governs identity verification services and the arrangements for using services such as DVS and FVS.
applicability: Applies if NDIA verifies identity documents, face images or credentials through national verification services.
source: Identity Verification Services Act 2023 and legislative instruments
publisher: Federal Register of Legislation / Attorney-General's Department

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: IVS participation agreements and published access policies
description: The Act requires agreements and policies related to identity verification services to be published and followed.
applicability: Applies to NDIA business owners and vendors integrating verification services.
source: Identity Verification Services register and guidance

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: DVS access and document verification
description: DVS checks whether identity document details match records held by the issuing authority.
applicability: Applies to participant, nominee, provider and workforce identity proofing where document checks are used.
source: Identity Verification Services register and guidance

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: FVS access and face verification
description: Face verification services compare a person's image against government-held records subject to strict controls.
applicability: Applies only where NDIA has lawful authority, approved service design and a completed PIA.
source: Identity Verification Services register and guidance

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: IVS privacy and security obligations
description: Access to IVS requires protection of personal information and compliance with service obligations.
applicability: Applies to verification transactions, logs, vendor support, API credentials and service administrators.
source: Identity Verification Services register and guidance

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: IVS audit and reporting
description: Use of identity verification services is subject to accountability, reporting and compliance expectations.
applicability: Applies to audit trails for verification requests, outcomes, operators and service accounts.
source: Identity Verification Services register and guidance

name: Identity Verification Services Act 2023
reference: Credential Protection Register alignment
description: Identity security arrangements include mechanisms to protect compromised or high-risk credentials.
applicability: Applies to account creation, recovery, high-risk access and fraud investigation.
source: Identity Verification Services register and guidance

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Experience Policy - mandated from 1 January 2025
description: The policy sets expectations for Australian Government digital services and is supported by standards including the Digital Service Standard.
applicability: Applies to participant, nominee, provider and public-facing NDIA digital identity services, subject to coverage status.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard - Leave no one behind
description: Services must be inclusive and support people with different circumstances, needs and access barriers.
applicability: Applies to account creation, MFA, proofing, nominee access, account recovery and provider onboarding.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard - Build trust in design
description: Services should be transparent, secure, privacy-aware and trustworthy.
applicability: Applies to CIAM consent screens, proofing notices, federation prompts and account recovery.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard - Do no harm
description: Services should identify and manage risks of harm, including misuse, exclusion and privacy impacts.
applicability: Applies to participants, nominees, support channels, representatives, providers and vulnerable users.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard - Connect services
description: Services should connect across channels and systems while protecting data and user trust.
applicability: Applies to SSO, myID/AGDIS, RAM, provider portals and partner integrations.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard - Monitor service performance
description: Services should measure performance, quality and user outcomes.
applicability: Applies to MFA success, lockouts, recovery, proofing drop-off, fraud, accessibility issues and nominee access errors.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Experience
reference: Digital Service Standard transition guidance
description: The Digital Service Standard applies progressively to new and existing services according to transition arrangements.
applicability: Applies to all new or materially changed NDIA digital identity services and existing public-facing services within coverage.
type: Mandatory digital service policy and standard

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: Digital Inclusion Standard
description: Government digital services must be inclusive, accessible and usable by people with diverse needs.
applicability: Applies to NDIA participant, nominee, provider and public digital identity services.
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: Digital Inclusion Standard criterion 4 - Make it accessible
description: Services must be accessible and align with legal and technical accessibility requirements including the latest WCAG.
applicability: Applies to login, account creation, MFA, recovery, consent, nomination and provider access workflows.
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.3.8 - Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
description: Authentication should not require cognitive function tests unless an alternative or assistance is provided.
applicability: Applies to participant and nominee login, account recovery, step-up authentication and provider access.
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: Australian Human Rights Commission - Equal access to digital goods and services
description: Digital services must be accessible to people with disability to reduce discrimination risk.
applicability: Applies to all public-facing and participant-facing identity journeys and support channels.
source: Equal access to digital goods and services guidance
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: Digital Inclusion Standard - Assisted digital support
description: Inclusive services should support users who cannot complete digital journeys independently.
applicability: Applies to assisted proofing, account recovery, nominee onboarding and contact-centre verification.
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: WCAG and MFA usability
description: Accessible authentication requires usable MFA, recovery and error handling.
applicability: Applies to SMS, authenticator apps, passkeys, hardware keys, voice, mail and assisted alternatives.
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: Digital Inclusion Standard
reference: Plain language and content accessibility
description: Digital inclusion requires understandable content and interactions.
applicability: Applies to privacy notices, consent screens, proofing instructions, error messages and recovery flows.
type: Accessibility and inclusion standard or guidance

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA Act s 16 - Duty to establish systems relating to risk and control
description: Accountable authorities must establish and maintain appropriate systems of risk oversight, risk management and internal control.
applicability: Applies to NDIA accountable authority governance and identity control assurance.
source: PGPA Act 2013 and Department of Finance resource management guidance

name: PGPA Act 2013
reference: PGPA framework - Proper use and management of public resources
description: Commonwealth officials are accountable for proper use and management of public resources.
applicability: Applies to workforce access, provider administration, payment functions and access to sensitive systems.
source: PGPA Act 2013 and Department of Finance resource management guidance

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
description: Entities should embed risk management into governance, decision-making and business processes.
applicability: Applies to identity architecture, exceptions, legacy systems, cloud identities and partner access.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy and Finance risk guidance

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Risk oversight and internal accountability
description: Entities must maintain systems to manage risk and internal accountability.
applicability: Applies to business role owners, data owners, system owners and identity control owners.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy and Finance risk guidance

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Segregation of duties as internal control
description: Internal controls should reduce opportunities for fraud, error and misuse.
applicability: Applies to claims, payments, provider registration, participant records, access administration and privileged change.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy and Finance risk guidance

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Fraud and integrity risk alignment
description: Risk controls should address fraud and integrity threats to public programs.
applicability: Applies to participant onboarding, nominee authority, provider representative access, payment changes and support desk recovery.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy and Finance risk guidance

name: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
reference: Risk acceptance and exceptions
description: Risk decisions should be made at the right level and documented.
applicability: Applies to any deviation from identity control requirements.
source: Commonwealth Risk Management Policy and Finance risk guidance

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Archives Act 1983 - Commonwealth records
description: Business information and data created or received by agencies are Commonwealth records and must be managed accordingly.
applicability: Applies to NDIA identity records, access requests, access reviews, logs, proofing outcomes, PAM sessions and federation transactions.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: NAA Information Management Standard
description: The standard applies to Australian Government business information in all formats and systems.
applicability: Applies to all NDIA identity repositories and audit evidence regardless of hosting model.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Information Management Standard Principle 4 - Suitably stored and preserved
description: Business information must be stored and preserved in a secure environment that prevents unauthorised access, alteration, removal or destruction.
applicability: Applies to audit logs, PAM recordings, identity governance workflows and approval evidence.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Information Management Standard Principle 6 - Accountable destruction or transfer
description: Business information must be accountably destroyed or transferred when authorised.
applicability: Applies to identity proofing evidence, former workforce accounts, nominee authority records, logs and decommissioned identity systems.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Records authorities
description: Records authorities are legal instruments that set retention and disposal requirements for records.
applicability: Applies to policy retention schedules and system purge configurations.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Data and datasets as records
description: Data and datasets retained in business systems are Commonwealth records and must be managed under the Archives Act.
applicability: Applies to IGA repositories, directories, access data warehouses and SIEM exports.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Archives Act 1983
reference: Audit accessibility and retrieval
description: Records must be findable and usable for business, accountability and legal purposes.
applicability: Applies to identity log retention, correlation identifiers and case management records.
source: Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards

name: Responsible AI
reference: Policy for responsible use of AI in government
description: Government agencies must use AI responsibly, safely and transparently according to mandatory policy actions and implementation timelines.
applicability: Applies to AI tools that access NDIA systems, participant data, provider records, credentials or access decisions.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI policy - Accountability
description: Agencies must assign accountability for AI implementation, use and governance.
applicability: Applies to AI service owners, data owners, system owners and sponsors of agentic workflows.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI policy - Strategy and oversight
description: Agencies must maintain oversight arrangements, including registers and governance of AI use cases.
applicability: Applies to AI chatbots, workflow agents, coding agents, decision-support tools and model integrations.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI use case impact assessment
description: In-scope AI use cases must be assessed and registered, including risk rating and ownership.
applicability: Applies before AI is used for identity proofing, fraud scoring, access recommendations, support triage or automated entitlement actions.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI policy - Staff training
description: Staff must receive training to use AI responsibly and safely.
applicability: Applies to administrators, developers, service teams, fraud teams, helpdesk and business users using AI with identity data.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: AI policy - Data governance, cyber, privacy and ethics alignment
description: Implementation guidance links AI use to data governance, cyber security, privacy and ethical obligations.
applicability: Applies to AI access to identity repositories, logs, entitlements, participant data and provider data.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: National AI assurance framework
description: The national framework supports consistent assurance of AI used by government.
applicability: Applies to AI identity use cases that affect access, proofing, fraud detection, support or participant services.
source: National framework for assurance of AI in government

name: Responsible AI
reference: Agentic system safety controls
description: Responsible AI governance requires controlling automated actions and escalation paths.
applicability: Applies to automated remediation, provisioning agents, workflow bots and AI service desk agents.
source: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Commonwealth Procurement Rules 2025
description: Procurement officials must meet CPR obligations, including value for money and proper use of public resources for covered entities.
applicability: Applies to NDIA procurement of identity platforms, CIAM, PAM, verification services, cloud services and managed providers, subject to CPR coverage and internal policy.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: CPRs - Security risk consideration
description: Government procurement guidance requires consideration and management of security risks, including cyber security in line with the PSPF.
applicability: Applies to all suppliers that host, administer, integrate with or access NDIA identity services or data.

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: DTA digital sourcing policies and whole-of-government arrangements
description: Digital sourcing must consider DTA policies, whole-of-government arrangements and connected policies.
applicability: Applies to SSO, CIAM, API gateways, Digital ID integrations, PAM, IGA and identity verification procurements.
source: Digital sourcing policy and whole-of-government arrangements

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Digital Sourcing ClauseBank
description: The ClauseBank provides contract clauses for digital sourcing arrangements.
applicability: Applies to software, cloud, managed service and identity verification provider contracts.

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Hosting Certification Framework
description: Certified hosting providers meet government expectations for data protection, ownership, transparency, privacy and security.
applicability: Applies to cloud-hosted directories, CIAM, PAM, identity analytics, logs and verification evidence.
source: Digital sourcing policy and whole-of-government arrangements

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Supplier administrator access
description: Supplier access must be controlled to reduce risk to government systems and data.
applicability: Applies to vendor support, managed services, implementation partners and break-glass support.

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Supplier lifecycle and exit
description: Procurement and contract management should address transition, records, data return and service continuity.
applicability: Applies to contract termination, service transition, system decommissioning and supplier offboarding.
source: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls

name: Commonwealth Procurement Rules and PGPA procurement controls
reference: Subcontractor and fourth-party access
description: Supplier arrangements should manage risks from subcontractors and service chains.
applicability: Applies to cloud operations, offshore support, implementation partners and managed service subcontractors.

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI Act 2018 - Critical infrastructure sectors and assets
description: The Act regulates critical infrastructure assets across prescribed sectors and imposes obligations on responsible entities.
applicability: Applies conditionally to NDIA identity services and suppliers where assets are covered by SOCI definitions or contract obligations.
source: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 guidance
publisher: Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre (Department of Home Affairs)
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI - Critical infrastructure risk management program (CIRMP)
description: Responsible entities for relevant assets must establish, maintain and comply with a written risk management program for material risks.
applicability: Applies if an NDIA-related identity asset or supplier is subject to CIRMP obligations.
source: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 guidance
publisher: Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre (Department of Home Affairs)
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI - Data storage or processing assets
description: Data storage and processing entities may have obligations related to business-critical data and access control.
applicability: Applies to identity SaaS, cloud hosting, logs, analytics platforms and managed service providers where SOCI criteria are met.
source: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 guidance
publisher: Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre (Department of Home Affairs)
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI - Access and control obligations for data storage
description: Guidance addresses access and control risks for data storage and processing services.
applicability: Applies conditionally to supplier administrators and NDIA administrators of identity services hosted in covered environments.
source: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 guidance
publisher: Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre (Department of Home Affairs)
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI - Cyber incident reporting obligations
description: Responsible entities for covered assets may have cyber incident reporting obligations.
applicability: Applies conditionally if identity services are part of, or materially affect, a covered asset.
source: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 guidance
publisher: Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre (Department of Home Affairs)
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: Cyber Security Act 2024 - Ransomware payment reporting
description: Ransomware payment reporting obligations commenced for certain entities and incidents from 30 May 2025.
applicability: Applies conditionally if NDIA or a supplier is a reporting business entity or payment is made in scope of the Act.
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
reference: SOCI and supplier flow-down
description: Responsible entities may need supplier cooperation to meet SOCI obligations.
applicability: Applies to managed service providers, identity SaaS, hosting providers and security monitoring providers.
source: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 guidance
publisher: Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre (Department of Home Affairs)
type: Critical infrastructure or cyber security legislation

name: Gatekeeper Public Key Infrastructure Framework
reference: Gatekeeper PKI Framework
description: The framework governs government use of digital keys and certificates to provide assurance of subscriber identity.
applicability: Applies to NDIA digital certificates, signing keys, mTLS client certificates, device certificates and service identities.

name: Gatekeeper Public Key Infrastructure Framework
reference: Gatekeeper - Subscriber identity assurance
description: Certificates bind a subscriber identity to a key under defined assurance arrangements.
applicability: Applies to non-human identities, system-to-system connections, provider API clients and privileged workstations.

name: Gatekeeper Public Key Infrastructure Framework
reference: Gatekeeper - Certificate lifecycle
description: PKI requires processes for request, approval, issuance, renewal, suspension and revocation.
applicability: Applies to TLS, SSO signing, code signing, API client authentication, device authentication and privileged admin certificates.

name: Gatekeeper Public Key Infrastructure Framework
reference: Gatekeeper - Private key protection
description: Private keys must be protected from compromise and unauthorised use.
applicability: Applies to SAML signing certificates, OIDC signing keys, mTLS keys, code signing keys and automation credentials.

name: Gatekeeper Public Key Infrastructure Framework
reference: Gatekeeper - Revocation and status checking
description: Certificate status and revocation mechanisms support trust decisions.
applicability: Applies to relying parties, federation gateways, API clients and device authentication.

name: Gatekeeper Public Key Infrastructure Framework
reference: Gatekeeper - Organisation and role certificates
description: Certificates can represent organisations or roles where appropriate controls exist.
applicability: Applies to provider organisations, partners, gateways and business representatives.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: OASIS SAML 2.0
description: SAML 2.0 provides standard federation assertions, bindings and profiles for exchanging authentication and attribute information.
applicability: Applies to SAML-based SSO, AGDIS data flows and legacy enterprise federation.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: OpenID Connect Core 1.0
description: OIDC defines an identity layer on OAuth 2.0 and use of ID tokens and claims to communicate end-user information.
applicability: Applies to OIDC identity providers, relying parties, mobile apps, portals and APIs.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: OAuth 2.1 and OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice RFC 9700
description: OAuth standards and security best current practice define secure authorization flows and deprecate less secure patterns.
applicability: Applies to OAuth clients, APIs, service-to-service integrations, mobile apps, web apps and AI agents.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: IETF SCIM RFC 7643 and RFC 7644
description: SCIM defines identity schemas and an HTTP-based protocol for provisioning and managing identities across domains.
applicability: Applies to workforce provisioning, SaaS app provisioning, provider user lifecycle and group management.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: W3C WebAuthn Level 3
description: WebAuthn enables strong public key credentials for web authentication.
applicability: Applies to participant, workforce, provider and privileged authentication where feasible and accessible.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: FIDO2 and passkeys
description: FIDO2 standards are used to deploy passkeys and phishing-resistant sign-in.
applicability: Applies to customer, workforce and administrator authentication roadmaps.

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: TLS 1.3 RFC 8446
description: TLS 1.3 secures client and server communications against eavesdropping, tampering and message forgery.
applicability: Applies to identity portals, APIs, federation endpoints, SCIM provisioning and mTLS service identities.
publisher: RFC Editor / Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)

name: Federation, authorization, provisioning and passkey technical standards
reference: OAuth token revocation, introspection and proof-of-possession profiles
description: IETF OAuth profiles support token lifecycle, validation and sender-constrained tokens.
applicability: Applies to APIs, service accounts, machine-to-machine access and agent workflows.

name: NIST SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines and SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture
reference: NIST SP 800-63-4 - Digital Identity Guidelines
description: The guidelines cover identity proofing, enrollment, authenticators, authentication protocols, federation and related assertions.
applicability: Use as a design reference for NDIA assurance levels, subordinate to Australian law and Digital ID requirements.
